summary_en: The bishop asked what he was doing and, seeing the mouse, said a man of his kind should not touch such a creature: let it go for seven pounds.
summary_zh: 主教问他在做什么，马纳维丹说：我在绞死一个小偷。

summary_en: Manawydan demanded one more thing: Llwyd's oath never again to enchant Dyfed nor take vengeance on Pryderi, Rhiannon or himself.
summary_zh: 马纳维丹说：我还要你发誓，以后永远不再对达费德施魔法，不再向普雷德里、里安农或我自己报复，为这件事报仇。

summary_en: One day after a feast at Arberth the four went up Gorsedd Arberth with their company — the mound where Pwyll had first seen Rhiannon.
summary_zh: 一天，他们四人在阿伯斯的宫殿里宴饮，饭后，带着随从们走上了阿伯斯的土丘——就是当年皮威尔第一次看见里安农的地方。

summary_en: 'We cannot go on like this,' said Manawydan; 'let us go to England and take up a craft to earn our living.' At Hereford they made saddles; Manawydan shaped them well and coloured them with blue enamel, as he had seen it done by Llasar Llaes Gyfnewid, and the townspeople bought no saddles but theirs.
summary_zh: 马纳维丹说：我们不能再这样过下去了，我们到英格兰去，学一门手艺来谋生吧。

summary_en: In a third town Pryderi asked what craft they would take up now.
summary_zh: 他们来到第三个城市，普雷德里问：我们这次做什么手艺？

summary_en: One morning Manawydan and Pryderi went hunting, and their hounds ran into a thicket and came back bristling in terror.
summary_zh: 一天早晨，马纳维丹和普雷德里带着猎犬去打猎，猎犬们冲进一片灌木丛，又惊恐地退了回来，毛都竖了起来。
title_en: The white boar and the strange fortress

summary_en: Inside the fortress there was no man, no house, no hounds or boar — only a fountain in the middle with a marble slab beside it, and on the slab a golden bowl hung by four chains that went up into the sky out of sight.
summary_zh: 普雷德里走进城堡，里面没有人，没有房屋，也没有他的猎犬和野猪，只在城堡中央有一口泉水，泉水边有一块大理石板，石板上放着一只金碗，金碗用四根链子吊着，链子一直延伸到天上，看不见尽头。
title_en: The golden bowl and the vanished fortress

summary_en: Only Manawydan and Pryderi's wife Cigfa were left at Arberth.
summary_zh: 阿伯斯的宫殿里，只剩下马纳维丹和普雷德里的妻子基格瓦两个人了。

summary_en: When the wheat was ripe Manawydan said he would reap the first croft next day; at dawn he found only bare straw, every ear cut off and carried away.
summary_zh: 麦子成熟了，马纳维丹去看第一块麦田，说：明天我就来收割。

summary_en: Of all the mice only one lagged behind, heavy and slow, and Manawydan caught it, put it in his glove, tied the mouth with a string, carried it home and hung the glove on a peg.
summary_zh: 那么多老鼠一下子都逃走了，只有一只老鼠跑得慢，因为它的身体又重又胖，落在了后面。

summary_en: Math son of Mathonwy was king of Gwynedd, and he could not live unless his feet were in the lap of a maiden, except when war prevented it.
summary_zh: 马索努伊的儿子马斯是格温内斯的国王。
title_zh: 持足少女与普雷德里的猪

summary_en: Gronw took Lleu's court and lands.
summary_zh: 格罗努占据了勒伊的宫殿和土地。

summary_en: Lleu was brought to Caer Dathyl, and all the best physicians of Gwynedd tended him until by the year's end he was whole again.
summary_zh: 勒伊被带到卡耳·达瑟尔，格温内斯所有最好的医生都来为他治疗，到了年底，他终于恢复了健康。

summary_en: Gronw Pebr fled to Penllyn and sent to ask whether Lleu would take land or gold and silver in compensation.
summary_zh: 格罗努·佩布尔逃回了他的领地彭林，派使者去问勒伊，愿不愿意接受土地、金银作为赔偿。

summary_en: Discovering the deceit, Pryderi marched north with the men of the south, and war broke out; Math mustered Gwynedd against him.
summary_zh: 普雷德里发现自己被骗了，带着南方的大军向北追来，战争爆发了。

summary_en: When Math returned and would put his feet in Goewin's lap, she told him to seek another maiden, for she was one no longer, and told him what had been done.
summary_zh: 马斯回到宫中，要把双脚放在戈尔文的膝上。

summary_en: Math needed a new footholder, and Gwydion proposed his sister Arianrhod daughter of Dôn.
summary_zh: 马斯需要一位新的持足少女，格威迪恩推荐了他的妹妹、多恩的女儿阿丽安萝德。

summary_en: One morning Gwydion heard a cry from the chest, opened it and found a little boy stretching out his arms.
summary_zh: 有一天早晨，格威迪恩在床上听见箱子里传出哭声，他打开箱子，看见一个小男孩伸出双臂。
title_en: The fair one with the skilful hand

summary_en: Arianrhod, tricked, laid a second destiny: he should never bear arms until she armed him herself.
summary_zh: 阿丽安萝德知道自己上当了，又下了第二个命运：除非我亲手给他武器，否则他永远不能拥有武器。

summary_en: Furious, Arianrhod laid a third destiny: he should never have a wife of the race that was now on the earth.
summary_zh: 阿丽安萝德愤怒至极，下了第三个命运：他永远不能娶这世上任何一个种族的女子为妻。

summary_en: One day while Lleu was visiting Math, Blodeuedd, walking in the court at Mur Castell, heard a horn and saw a weary stag pass with hounds and huntsmen after it: Gronw Pebr, lord of Penllyn, was hunting.
summary_zh: 一天，勒伊去拜访马斯，布罗黛维德独自留在穆尔·卡斯泰尔。

summary_en: That night Blodeuedd was silent, and when Lleu asked why, she said she feared he would die before her.
summary_zh: 那天晚上，布罗黛维德一言不发，勒伊问她为什么不高兴。
title_en: Neither in a house nor out of doors

summary_en: In the Han dynasty there was a man of Qiancheng named Dong Yong.
summary_zh: 汉朝的时候，千乘县有一个人叫董永。
title_en: Dong Yong and the Weaving Maiden

summary_en: Ziyu, youngest daughter of King Fuchai of Wu, was eighteen, outstanding in talent and beauty.
summary_zh: 吴王夫差的小女儿名叫紫玉，十八岁，才华和容貌都很出众。

summary_en: Song Dingbo of Nanyang, when he was young, was walking at night and met a ghost.
summary_zh: 南阳有个叫宋定伯的人，年轻的时候，有一次夜里赶路，遇到了一个鬼。

summary_en: In Minzhong of Eastern Yue there is a ridge called Yongling, tens of li high, and in a valley to its northwest lived a great serpent seven or eight zhang long and more than ten spans round, which the local people dreaded.
summary_zh: 东越闽中有一座庸岭，高几十里，岭的西北山谷里住着一条大蛇，长七八丈，粗十几围，当地人都很害怕。

summary_en: In the time of Sun Quan there lived in Jinan in Xiangyang a man named Li Xinchun who kept a dog called Black Dragon.
summary_zh: 三国孙权的时候，襄阳纪南有一个人叫李信纯，家里养了一条狗，名叫黑龙，他非常喜爱这条狗，走到哪里都带着它，吃饭喝酒的时候也总分给它一份。
title_en: The tomb of the faithful dog

summary_en: Gan Jiang and Mo Ye of Chu forged swords for the king of Chu, and it took them three years.
summary_zh: 楚国的干将和莫邪为楚王铸剑，用了三年才铸成。

summary_en: The king of Chu dreamed of a boy with a foot's breadth between his brows who said he would take vengeance, and the king offered a thousand pieces of gold for him.
summary_zh: 楚王梦见一个少年，两眉之间宽一尺，说要来报仇。
title_en: The Tomb of the Three Kings

summary_en: In the Han dynasty Fan Shi, styled Juqing, of Jinxiang in Shanyang, was a close friend of Zhang Shao of Runan, styled Yuanbo.
summary_zh: 汉朝的范式，字巨卿，是山阳金乡人，和汝南的张劭是好朋友，张劭字元伯。

summary_en: In the Han dynasty there was in Donghai commandery a filial daughter-in-law who served her mother-in-law with great devotion.
summary_zh: 汉朝的时候，东海郡有一位孝顺的媳妇，奉养婆婆非常尽心。

summary_en: Han Ping, a retainer of King Kang of Song, married a woman of the He family who was very beautiful, and King Kang took her from him.
summary_zh: 宋康王的舍人韩凭，娶了何氏为妻，何氏非常美丽，宋康王就把她夺了去。

summary_en: Yi obtained from the Queen Mother of the West the drug of deathlessness, and his wife Heng'e — later more often written Chang'e — stole it and fled to the moon.
summary_zh: 后羿向西王母求得了长生不死的药，他的妻子姮娥——后来人们多写作嫦娥——偷了这药，奔向月亮。

summary_en: An old tale says: in high antiquity a man went far away to war, leaving at home only his daughter and a stallion, which she tended herself.
summary_zh: 古老的传说讲：远古的时候，有一个人出远门去征战，家里没有别人，只剩下一个女儿和一匹公马，女儿亲自喂养这匹马。
title_en: The girl who became a silkworm

summary_en: A man of Xinyu county in Yuzhang saw six or seven women in a field, all in robes of feathers, not knowing that they were birds.
summary_zh: 豫章郡新喻县有一个男子，看见田里有六七个女子，都穿着羽毛做的衣服，他不知道她们其实是鸟。

summary_en: Lemminkäinen, also called Ahti and Kaukomieli, was a handsome young man with ruddy cheeks and fine hair, but wild and reckless, his eyes always roving after the maidens.
summary_zh: 勒明凯宁又叫阿赫蒂、考科米耶利，是一个英俊的年轻人，脸颊红润，头发漂亮，可是性情放荡不羁，眼睛总是在少女们身上打转。

summary_en: The blind herdsman threw the dying Lemminkäinen into the black river of Tuonela, and the current swept him towards the roaring falls.
summary_zh: 盲眼牧人把奄奄一息的勒明凯宁扔进了图奥内拉的黑河里，河水把他卷向汹涌的瀑布。
title_en: The pieces in the black river

summary_en: At home, Lemminkäinen's mother watched the brush every day.
summary_zh: 在勒明凯宁的家里，母亲每天都看着那把梳子。

summary_en: Weeping, the mother went to the smith Ilmarinen and asked for a rake with copper teeth a hundred fathoms long and a handle five hundred fathoms long, and Ilmarinen forged it.
summary_zh: 母亲哭着去找铁匠伊尔马里宁，请他打一把耙子：铜的耙齿要一百寻长，耙柄要五百寻长。
title_en: The copper rake and the bee

summary_en: One evening the maidens were dancing in a forest glade with Kyllikki leading them.
summary_zh: 有一天傍晚，少女们在林间空地上跳舞，基利基跳在最前面。

summary_en: The days went by, and Lemminkäinen often went out fishing.
summary_zh: 日子一天天过去，勒明凯宁常常出门去打鱼。

summary_en: His mother begged him: 'Do not go to Pohjola.
summary_zh: 母亲苦苦劝他：不要去波赫约拉，那里的拉普兰巫师会用歌声把你唱进火里、唱进冰里，你一个人去会丢掉性命的。

summary_en: Arriving in Pohjola, Lemminkäinen went into Louhi's hall, which was full of sorcerers and singers playing and singing; they ignored the stranger.
summary_zh: 勒明凯宁来到波赫约拉，走进洛希的大厅，那里坐满了巫师和歌者，弹琴的弹琴，唱歌的唱歌。
title_en: The sorcerers and the blind herdsman

summary_en: Lemminkäinen asked Louhi for her daughter.
summary_zh: 勒明凯宁向洛希求娶她的女儿。

summary_en: Lemminkäinen mended his skis, and this time, instead of boasting, he prayed to the forest gods.
summary_zh: 勒明凯宁修好了滑雪板，这一次他不再夸口，而是向森林之神祈祷。

summary_en: Louhi said: 'Go and bridle the brown gelding of Hiisi, which runs on Hiisi's meadows breathing fire from its nostrils and smoke from its mouth.' Lemminkäinen set out with a golden halter and a silver bridle.
summary_zh: 洛希说：你去把希西那匹棕色的骟马套上笼头，它在希西的原野上奔跑，鼻孔里喷着火，嘴里冒着烟。

summary_en: Louhi said: 'Go to the black river of Tuonela, and with a single arrow shoot the swan there; then my daughter shall be yours.' Tuonela was the land of the dead, and the black river lay in the realm of Tuoni, lord of the dead.
summary_zh: 洛希说：你去图奥内拉的黑河上，只射一箭，射死那里的天鹅，我就把女儿给你。

summary_en: In the oldest times there was a maiden, daughter of the air, named Ilmatar.
summary_zh: 在最古老的时候，有一位少女，她是大气的女儿，名叫伊尔玛塔尔。
title_en: The daughter of the air and the duck's eggs

summary_en: Driving south in his sledge, Väinämöinen heard the sound of a loom above him.
summary_zh: 万奈莫宁赶着雪橇往南走，忽然听见头顶传来织布机的声音。
title_en: The maiden on the rainbow and the axe

summary_en: Bleeding, Väinämöinen drove on in search of a healer.
summary_zh: 万奈莫宁流着血，赶着雪橇去找能治伤的人。

summary_en: Back home, Väinämöinen urged the smith Ilmarinen to go north, forge the Sampo and win the maiden of Pohjola.
summary_zh: 万奈莫宁回到家，劝铁匠伊尔马里宁到北方去锻造三宝、娶波赫约拉的少女。

summary_en: With the world given shape, Ilmatar floated on for many years and began to form the land: where she pointed her hand, headlands rose; where she pressed with her foot, deep pools for the fish were made; where she lay on her side, smooth shores appeared; where her feet touched, bays were formed, and where her head rested, harbours.
summary_zh: 世界有了形状，伊尔玛塔尔又在海上漂了许多年，开始塑造大地的样子：她把手一指，就出现了岬角；用脚一踩，就有了鱼儿栖息的深坑；侧身一躺，就形成了平滑的海岸；她脚踏过的地方成了海湾，头枕过的地方成了港口。

summary_en: Coming ashore, Väinämöinen saw that the land was bare and nothing grew.
summary_zh: 万奈莫宁上了岸，看见大地光秃秃的，什么也不长。
title_en: The sowing and the great oak

summary_en: The fame of Väinämöinen's songs and wisdom spread far and wide.
summary_zh: 万奈莫宁的歌声和智慧传遍了四方。

summary_en: Sunk in the swamp, Joukahainen was terrified and began to beg.
summary_zh: 约卡海宁陷在沼泽里，吓坏了，开始求饶。

summary_en: Aino went into the woods to break birch twigs for a bath-whisk and met Väinämöinen there.
summary_zh: 艾诺到林中去折桦树枝做浴帚，在那里遇见了万奈莫宁。

summary_en: Hearing that Aino was dead, Väinämöinen grieved day and night.
summary_zh: 万奈莫宁听说艾诺死了，日夜悲伤。
title_en: The fish and the lost bride

summary_en: Väinämöinen mounted a horse as light as a pea-stalk and set off over the waves for northern Pohjola.
summary_zh: 万奈莫宁骑上一匹轻得像豆秆一样的马，踏着海浪向北方的波赫约拉出发。

summary_en: Väinämöinen drifted on the sea for many days, cold and hungry, with no shore in sight.
summary_zh: 万奈莫宁在海上漂了许多天，又冷又饿，看不到岸。

summary_en: Once, the poem begins, a mother raised a brood of chicks: one was carried to Russia, one to Karelia, and one stayed at home — with such an image the singer opens the tale of two brothers.
summary_zh: 从前，有一位母亲养大了一窝小鸡，一只被带到了俄罗斯，一只被带到了卡累利阿，还有一只留在家里——诗人用这样的比喻开始讲述两兄弟的故事。

summary_en: The maiden understood everything and was overcome with grief.
summary_zh: 少女明白了一切，悲痛欲绝。

summary_en: As he made ready for war, Kullervo asked each of his family: 'When I die, will you weep for me?' His father said: 'No; I will beget a better son.' His brother said: 'No; I will find a better brother.' His sister said: 'No; I will find a better brother.' Only his mother said: 'I will weep for you, in the house and in the fields and everywhere, until my tears run dry.' Kullervo set out.
summary_zh: 库勒沃准备出征，他一个个地问家人：我死了，你们会为我哭泣吗？

summary_en: Kullervo came home to find the house empty and the hearth cold; father, mother, brother and sister were all dead.
summary_zh: 库勒沃回到家里，家中空无一人，炉灶冰冷，父亲、母亲、兄弟和姐妹都已经死去。

summary_en: In Untamo's house the woman bore a son.
summary_zh: 那个女子在温塔莫家里生下了一个男孩，母亲给他取名叫库勒沃，温塔莫的人则叫他“战争之子”。

summary_en: First Untamo had a barrel made, shut Kullervo inside and threw him into the lake.
summary_zh: 温塔莫先叫人做了一只木桶，把库勒沃装进去，扔进了湖里。
title_en: The child who could not be killed

summary_en: Untamo set Kullervo to work.
summary_zh: 温塔莫给库勒沃派活。

summary_en: Ilmarinen's wife — the maiden of Pohjola of old, now mistress of the smith's house — looked at the new slave and thought: let him herd the cattle.
summary_zh: 伊尔马里宁的妻子，就是当年那位波赫约拉的少女，如今是铁匠家的女主人。
title_en: The bread with a stone in it

summary_en: At noon Kullervo sat down on a hillside, took out the mistress's loaf and cut into it; the blade struck the stone in the middle and snapped.
summary_zh: 到了中午，库勒沃坐在山坡上，拿出主妇给的面包，用刀一切，刀刃碰到了中间的石头，啪的一声折断了。

summary_en: At evening Kullervo drove his 'cattle' into the byre, the horn sounding far and wide.
summary_zh: 傍晚，库勒沃把那群“牛”赶进了牛栏，号角声响彻四方。

summary_en: Kullervo wandered in the forest, full of grief and anger.
summary_zh: 库勒沃在森林里游荡，心中充满了悲伤和愤怒。

summary_en: Back home, Kullervo tried to help his parents but could do nothing right.
summary_zh: 回到家里，库勒沃想帮父母干活，却什么也干不好：父亲让他划船，他把船桨划断了，把船底都划穿了；让他撒网捕鱼，他把水搅成了泥浆，把渔网撕成了碎片。

summary_en: Ilmarinen grieved long for his lost wife.
summary_zh: 伊尔马里宁失去了妻子，悲伤了很久。
title_en: The sword and the weeping boat

summary_en: Louhi in her fury worked magic to pursue the heroes.
summary_zh: 洛希大怒，施展魔法追赶英雄们。
title_en: Fog, the sea monster and the storm

summary_en: Louhi built a great war-ship, put a hundred warriors aboard with swords, bows and arrows, and led the pursuit herself.
summary_zh: 洛希造了一艘巨大的战船，让上百名武士带着刀剑和弓箭上船，亲自率领他们追赶。

summary_en: Though she had lost her talons, Louhi would not give up.
summary_zh: 洛希虽然失去了爪子，却不肯罢休。

summary_en: As the boat passed a headland, someone on the shore called out: 'Who is sailing on the sea?' It was Lemminkäinen.
summary_zh: 船经过一座岬角时，岸上有人在喊：是谁在海上航行？

summary_en: The boat ran into a stretch of wild river, threading between rapids and falls.
summary_zh: 船驶进一段湍急的河道，在急流和瀑布之间穿行。

summary_en: Looking at the heap of bones, Väinämöinen wondered what they might become.
summary_zh: 万奈莫宁看着那堆鱼骨，心想：这些骨头要是做成一件东西，会是什么样子？

summary_en: Väinämöinen washed his hands, sat down on a stone of singing, set the kantele on his knee and plucked the strings with his fingers.
summary_zh: 万奈莫宁洗净双手，坐在一块歌唱的石头上，把康特勒琴放在膝上，用手指拨动琴弦。

summary_en: Everyone who heard the music wept: the young and the old, men and women, even the little children.
summary_zh: 所有听见琴声的人都哭了：年轻的人哭了，老人哭了，男人和女人都哭了，连小孩子也哭了。

summary_en: At last the boat reached Pohjola.
summary_zh: 船终于到了波赫约拉。

summary_en: The heroes came to the copper mountain of Pohjola, where the Sampo was locked behind nine doors.
summary_zh: 英雄们来到波赫约拉的铜山前，三宝就锁在山里的九道门后。

summary_en: The boat sailed smoothly over the sea with the Sampo hidden in the hold, and the three heroes were glad.
summary_zh: 船在海上平稳地航行，三宝藏在船舱里，三位英雄心里都很高兴。

summary_en: The Pāṇḍavas had spent twelve years in the forest and a thirteenth in hiding at the court of Virāṭa; by the terms of the dice game they should now have their kingdom back.
summary_zh: 般度五子在森林里过了十二年，又在毗罗吒国隐姓埋名地度过了第十三年，按照当年掷骰子时的约定，他们应该收回自己的王国。

summary_en: Bhīma and Duryodhana fought with iron maces by the lake, the clash striking sparks and sounding like thunder.
summary_zh: 怖军和难敌拿着铁杵在湖边对战，两人的杵碰撞时迸出火花，声音像霹雳一样。

summary_en: Of the Kauravas only three remained alive: Droṇa's son Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman.
summary_zh: 俱卢族只剩下三个人还活着：德罗纳的儿子马嘶、慈悯和成铠。

summary_en: The next morning Draupadī learned that all five of her sons were dead and, beside herself with grief, vowed to fast to death unless Aśvatthāman were punished.
summary_zh: 第二天清晨，黑公主得知五个儿子都被杀死，悲痛欲绝，发誓说：如果马嘶不受惩罚，我就绝食而死。

summary_en: The armies drew up on the field of Kurukṣetra, the plain called the field of dharma: seven armies of the Pāṇḍavas, eleven of the Kauravas, banners darkening the sun, drums and conches shaking heaven and earth.
summary_zh: 两军在俱卢之野——一片被称为“正法之野”的平原——上摆开了阵势：般度族七支大军，俱卢族十一支大军，旌旗蔽日，战鼓和螺号响彻天地。

summary_en: The first commander of the Kauravas was old Bhīṣma, son of the river goddess Gaṅgā, who in his youth had vowed for his father's sake never to marry or claim the throne, and had been granted the boon of choosing the hour of his own death.
summary_zh: 俱卢族的第一位统帅是年老的毗湿摩。

summary_en: After Bhīṣma fell, Droṇa took command of the Kauravas.
summary_zh: 毗湿摩倒下以后，德罗纳做了俱卢族的统帅。

summary_en: When Arjuna returned to camp and learned that his son had fallen and that Jayadratha had held back the rescuers at the breach, he was beside himself with grief and vowed before all: 'Before sunset tomorrow I will kill Jayadratha; if I fail, I will enter the fire.' When the news reached the Kauravas, Jayadratha in terror wanted to flee, but Droṇa promised to protect him and hid him at the very rear of the host behind array upon array.
summary_zh: 阿周那回到营地，得知儿子战死，又听说是胜车在阵口挡住了救兵，悲痛欲绝，当众立下誓言：明天日落之前，我一定要杀死胜车；如果做不到，我就投火自焚。

summary_en: That night the fighting did not stop; the armies fought on in the dark by torchlight.
summary_zh: 那一夜，战斗没有停止，两军举着火把在黑暗中继续厮杀。

summary_en: On the fifteenth day Droṇa was invincible, slaying hosts of Pāṇḍava soldiers with his divine weapons.
summary_zh: 第十五天，德罗纳在战场上无人能敌，用神兵杀死了大批般度族的士兵。

summary_en: After Droṇa's death Karṇa took command of the Kauravas.
summary_zh: 德罗纳死后，迦尔纳做了俱卢族的统帅。

summary_en: On the eighteenth day Śalya, last commander of the Kauravas, was slain by Yudhiṣṭhira himself, and Śakuni, who had rigged the dice, was slain by Sahadeva, youngest of the Pāṇḍavas.
summary_zh: 第十八天，沙利耶做了俱卢族最后一位统帅，被坚战亲手杀死；那个在掷骰时设下骗局的沙恭尼，也被般度五子中最小的偶天杀死。

summary_en: Yudhiṣṭhira, eldest of the Pāṇḍava brothers, had lost his kingdom at dice and gone into exile in the forest with his four brothers and their wife Draupadī, to spend twelve years there and a thirteenth in hiding.
summary_zh: 般度族的长兄坚战在掷骰中输掉了王国，带着四个弟弟和妻子黑公主流放到森林里，要在那里度过十二年，再隐姓埋名过一年。

summary_en: After leaving his wife, Nala saw a great fire in the forest, and from it a voice cried: 'Nala, come and save me!' He went into the fire and found a huge serpent coiled there, the nāga king Karkoṭaka, who said: 'Cursed by the sage Nārada, I cannot move; only you can save me.
summary_zh: 那罗离开妻子以后，在森林里看见一场大火，火中有声音喊道：那罗，快来救我！

summary_en: As Bāhuka, Nala served Ṛtuparṇa at Ayodhyā as his charioteer and master of the stables.
summary_zh: 那罗以巴胡迦的名字在阿逾陀做了利图帕尔纳的车夫，掌管马厩。

summary_en: Hearing Parṇāda's report, Damayantī understood and devised a plan.
summary_zh: 达摩衍蒂听了帕尔纳达的报告，心里明白了，就想出一个办法。
title_en: The hundred-yojana drive and the science of dice
title_zh: 百由旬的车程与骰子的学问

summary_en: Ṛtuparṇa's chariot thundered into the capital of Vidarbha, the noise shaking the palace, and Damayantī knew at once that only Nala drove like that.
summary_zh: 利图帕尔纳的车隆隆地驶进毗陀婆的都城，车声震动了宫殿，达摩衍蒂一听就知道，只有那罗能把车驾得这样快。

summary_en: Learning the truth, Ṛtuparṇa asked Nala's pardon; Nala taught him the science of horses, and they parted friends.
summary_zh: 利图帕尔纳知道了真相，向那罗道歉，那罗也把驾驭马匹的学问教给了他，两人友好地分别。

summary_en: Long ago there was a king of the Nishadhas named Nala, son of Vīrasena.
summary_zh: 从前，尼沙陀国有一位国王，名叫那罗，是英雄维罗森那的儿子。

summary_en: Damayantī grew restless and pale.
summary_zh: 达摩衍蒂从此心神不宁，日渐消瘦。

summary_en: The gods made Nala invisible, and he passed unhindered into the inner palace of Vidarbha.
summary_zh: 天神让那罗隐去身形，他一路畅通无阻地走进了毗陀婆王宫的后宫。

summary_en: The day of the svayaṃvara came.
summary_zh: 选婿大会的日子到了。

summary_en: The four gods were not angry but pleased, and each gave Nala two boons: Indra, that he would see the gods with his own eyes at sacrifices and reach the heavenly worlds; Agni, that fire would appear whenever he wished and that he would have worlds bright as fire; Yama, skill in fine cooking and steadfastness in dharma; Varuṇa, that water would appear whenever he wished, and garlands that never faded.
summary_zh: 四位天神没有生气，他们都很高兴，各自赐给那罗两个恩惠：因陀罗让他在祭祀时能亲眼看见天神，并能到达天界；阿耆尼让他想要火的时候火就会出现，并让他拥有像火一样光明的世界；阎摩赐给他烹调的美味和对正法的坚定；伐楼那让他想要水的时候水就会出现，并赐给他永不凋谢的花环。

summary_en: Kali came to Nishadha and waited for Nala to commit some fault.
summary_zh: 迦利来到尼沙陀，等着那罗犯下一个过失。

summary_en: Pushkara proclaimed that anyone who sheltered Nala would die.
summary_zh: 补湿迦罗下令：谁要是收留那罗，就处死谁。

summary_en: Damayantī woke to find her husband gone and searched the forest weeping and calling.
summary_zh: 达摩衍蒂醒来，不见了丈夫，哭喊着在森林里四处寻找。

summary_en: In the forest Yudhiṣṭhira asked the sage Mārkaṇḍeya: 'Has there ever been a woman as virtuous and as devoted to her husband as our Draupadī?' 'There has, king,' said Mārkaṇḍeya; 'hear the story of Sāvitrī.
summary_zh: 坚战在森林里问仙人摩根德耶：世上可曾有过像我们的黑公主那样贤德、那样忠于丈夫的女子？

summary_en: Sorrowing, Sāvitrī followed Yama.
summary_zh: 莎维德丽悲伤地跟在阎摩身后走去。

summary_en: As she walked Sāvitrī spoke on: 'To meet the good even once is to be sought; friendship with the good is above all things; so one should keep company with the good.' 'Your words profit even the wise,' said Yama; 'ask a second boon, except Satyavān's life.' 'Let my father-in-law regain his lost kingdom and never stray from dharma.' Yama granted it and again bade her return.
summary_zh: 莎维德丽一边走，一边继续说话：与善人相处，哪怕只有一次，也是值得追求的；和善人交朋友，比什么都可贵，所以人应该和善人在一起。

summary_en: Yama loosened the noose and departed, telling Sāvitrī that Satyavān would live four hundred years and share happiness with her.
summary_zh: 阎摩解开了绳索，带着灵魂离去，并告诉莎维德丽，萨谛梵将活四百年，与她一起享受幸福。
title_en: The way home through the night

summary_en: That same day the blind king Dyumatsena suddenly regained his sight.
summary_zh: 就在那天，盲王迪尤摩特舍那忽然重见了光明。

summary_en: Aśvapati said: 'Goddess, I ask only for offspring; it was for the continuance of my line that I kept these vows.
summary_zh: 马主王说：女神啊，我所求的只是子嗣，为了延续家族，我才守戒修行。

summary_en: Sāvitrī came of age to marry, but her beauty and radiance daunted everyone, and no one dared to ask for her hand.
summary_zh: 莎维德丽到了出嫁的年纪，可她的美丽和光彩让所有的人都望而却步，竟然没有一个人敢来向她求婚。

summary_en: Some time later Sāvitrī returned.
summary_zh: 过了一些日子，莎维德丽回来了。

summary_en: Aśvapati said to his daughter: 'Sāvitrī, go and choose another husband.
summary_zh: 马主王听了，对女儿说：莎维德丽，你去另选一个丈夫吧，萨谛梵这个缺点盖过了他所有的美德，一年之后他就会死去。

summary_en: On an auspicious day Aśvapati, with brahmins and priests and chariots laden with things for the wedding, brought Sāvitrī to the hermitage where Dyumatsena lived.
summary_zh: 马主王选了一个吉日，带着婆罗门和祭司，用车载着结婚的用品，带着莎维德丽来到迪尤摩特舍那所住的净修林。

summary_en: The days went by in the happy hermitage life, but Nārada's words weighed on Sāvitrī's heart, and day and night she counted the days, telling no one.
summary_zh: 日子一天天过去，在快乐的净修林生活里，莎维德丽的心中却始终压着那罗陀的话，日日夜夜地数着日子。

summary_en: That day Satyavān shouldered his axe to go into the forest for wood and fruit.
summary_zh: 那一天，萨谛梵扛起斧头，要到林中去砍柴、采果子。

summary_en: Satyavān gathered fruit and filled his basket, then began to cut wood.
summary_zh: 萨谛梵采了果子，装满了篮子，又开始砍柴。

summary_en: The Kojiki proper opens at the time when heaven and earth first began.
summary_zh: 《古事记》的正文从天地开辟写起。

summary_en: Terrified at the sight, Izanagi turned and fled.
summary_zh: 伊邪那岐看见这副情景，吓得转身就逃。
title_en: The Ugly Females of Yomi and the three peaches

summary_en: Last of all Izanami herself came in pursuit.
summary_zh: 最后，伊邪那美亲自追来了。

summary_en: 'I have been to a hideous and polluted land,' said Izanagi, 'so I must purify my body.' He came to the plain of Ahagi by the river-mouth of Tachibana in Himuka in Tsukushi and performed purification.
summary_zh: 伊邪那岐说：我去了一个丑恶污秽的国家，必须洗净我的身体。
title_en: Purification and the three noble children

summary_en: Next came into being Kuni-no-toko-tachi and Toyo-kumo-nu, who also came alone and hid their persons.
summary_zh: 接着出现的是国之常立神和丰云野神，他们也是独自出现、隐去身形的神。

summary_en: All the heavenly deities commanded Izanagi and Izanami to make, consolidate and give birth to the drifting land — three tasks that the rest of the story works through one by one — and granted them a jewelled spear, the Ame-no-nuhoko.
summary_zh: 天上的众神一齐命令伊邪那岐和伊邪那美：去把这片漂浮的国土整治好，使它坚固，把它生出来。

summary_en: On the island they set up a heavenly pillar and built a hall eight fathoms wide.
summary_zh: 两位神在岛上竖起了一根天之御柱，又建起一座八寻殿——“寻”是两臂张开的长度，八寻就是极言其宽大。
title_en: The heavenly pillar and the leech-child

summary_en: The two took counsel: 'The children we have borne are not good.
summary_zh: 两位神商量说：我们生的孩子不好，应该去问问天上的众神。

summary_en: Having borne the lands, Izanagi and Izanami went on to bear deities, and the text records each name: Oho-koto-oshi-wo, Iha-tsuchi-biko, Iha-su-hime, Oho-to-hi-wake, Ame-no-fuki-wo, Oho-ya-biko, Kaza-mo-tsu-wake-no-oshi-wo; the great sea deity Oho-wata-tsu-mi; the river-mouth deities Haya-aki-tsu-hiko and Haya-aki-tsu-hime, who in turn bore deities of foam and of the water's surface; the wind deity Shina-tsu-hiko, the tree deity Kuku-no-chi, the great mountain deity Oho-yama-tsu-mi and the moor goddess Kaya-nu-hime, also called Nu-dzu-chi, who together bore deities of earth, mist and valleys.
summary_zh: 生完了国土，伊邪那岐和伊邪那美又接着生神。

summary_en: Last of all Izanami bore the fire deity Kagutsuchi, also called Hi-no-yagi-haya-wo and Hi-no-kaga-biko.
summary_zh: 最后，伊邪那美生下了火之迦具土神，也叫火之夜艺速男神、火之炫毘古神。

summary_en: Izanagi cried: 'Oh my beloved younger sister!
summary_zh: 伊邪那岐悲痛地说：我亲爱的妹妹啊，我怎么能用你换来这一个孩子！
title_en: Mourning and the slaying of the fire deity

summary_en: Wishing to see his wife again, Izanagi followed her to the Land of Yomi.
summary_zh: 伊邪那岐思念妻子，追到了黄泉国。
title_en: Yomi: do not look at me

summary_en: After telling how Susanoo built his palace in Izumo and married Kushinada-hime, the Kojiki lists his descendants: their son Yashima-jinumi, and so on down the generations to Ame-no-fuyu-kinu, who married Sashikuni-waka-hime, daughter of the great deity of Sashikuni, and fathered the hero of this part — the sixth generation from Susanoo.
summary_zh: 《古事记》在讲完须佐之男在出云建宫、娶栉名田比卖之后，接着列出了他的子孙：须佐之男和栉名田比卖生下八岛士奴美神，此后一代代往下传，传到天之冬衣神，天之冬衣神娶了刺国大神的女儿刺国若比卖，生下的就是这一部故事的主人公——从须佐之男往下数，正好是第六代。
title_en: The five names of the Master of the Great Land

summary_en: As Yachihoko, the Deity of Eight Thousand Spears, he went to distant Koshi to woo Princess Nunakawa.
summary_zh: 以八千矛神为名的大国主，又到遥远的越国去向沼河比卖求婚。
title_en: The songs of the Deity of Eight Thousand Spears

summary_en: Once, at Cape Miho in Izumo, Ōkuninushi saw a deity riding the crests of the waves in a little boat made from a seed-pod of the kagami plant, clothed in the whole stripped skin of some small creature — the character is read by some as a goose and by others as a moth.
summary_zh: 有一天，大国主在出云的美保岬，看见一位神乘着用萝藦豆荚做成的小船，踏着浪花漂过来，身上穿着用整张剥下来的小动物的皮做的衣服——原文的字一说是鹅，一说指飞蛾。

summary_en: With Sukuna-bikona gone, Ōkuninushi said in sorrow: 'How can I make this land alone?
summary_zh: 少名毘古那走了，大国主忧愁地说：我一个人怎么能把这片国土造好呢？

summary_en: Amaterasu declared that the Luxuriant Reed-Plains Land of Fresh Rice-Ears should be ruled by her son Ame-no-oshi-ho-mimi.
summary_zh: 天照大神说：丰苇原的瑞穗国应该由我的儿子天忍穗耳命来统治。

summary_en: Last, the deities sent Takemikazuchi, with Ame-no-tori-fune.
summary_zh: 众神最后派出了建御雷神，由天鸟船神陪同。
title_en: Takemikazuchi and the yielding of the land

summary_en: The Eighty Deities all wished to marry Princess Yakami of Inaba, and set out together, making Ōnamuji carry their bag like a servant.
summary_zh: 八十神都想娶稻羽的八上比卖，一起出发去求婚，让大穴牟迟背着袋子，像仆人一样跟在后面。

summary_en: Princess Yakami told the Eighty Deities: 'I will not listen to you.
summary_zh: 八上比卖果然对八十神说：我不听你们的话，我要嫁给大穴牟迟。
title_en: The red boar of Mount Tema

summary_en: Seeing him alive again, the Eighty Deities set another trap.
summary_zh: 八十神看见他又活了，再次设下圈套。

summary_en: The Nether-Distant-Land, the mother's land that Susanoo had once wept to go to, was now his dwelling.
summary_zh: 根之坚洲国——张伯伦译作“幽远之国”——就是当年须佐之男哭着要去的母亲之国，如今他住在这里。

summary_en: The next night Susanoo put him in a room full of centipedes and wasps.
summary_zh: 第二天晚上，须佐之男又让他睡在一间满是蜈蚣和马蜂的屋子里。
title_en: The room of centipedes and wasps

summary_en: Next Susanoo shot a whizzing arrow into a great moor and sent Ōnamuji to fetch it.
summary_zh: 须佐之男又把一支鸣镝——箭头上装着中空的响器、射出去会呼啸作响的箭——射进一片大草原，命令大穴牟迟去把箭找回来。
title_en: The burning moor and the mouse

summary_en: Susanoo took him back into the house, called him into a great room eight fathoms wide, and made him pick the lice from his head.
summary_zh: 须佐之男把大穴牟迟带回家里，叫进一间八寻宽的大屋子，让他替自己捉头上的虱子。

summary_en: While Susanoo slept, Ōnamuji tied his hair to the rafters of the room, blocked the door with a rock that would take five hundred men to move, took his wife Suseri-bime on his back, and fled carrying Susanoo's great sword of life, his bow and arrows of life, and his heavenly speaking lute.
summary_zh: 大穴牟迟趁须佐之男睡着，把他的头发一缕缕绑在屋子的椽子上，用一块要五百个人才拉得动的大石头堵住屋门，背起妻子须势理毘卖，带上须佐之男的生太刀、生弓矢和天诏琴，逃了出去。
title_en: The sword of life, the bow and the speaking lute
title_zh: 生太刀、生弓矢与天诏琴

summary_en: Takemikazuchi went back up and reported that the Central Land of Reed-Plains had been pacified.
summary_zh: 建御雷神回到天上，报告苇原中国已经平定。

summary_en: A maid of the sea deity's daughter Toyotama-bime came to the well with a jewelled vessel to draw water.
summary_zh: 海神的女儿丰玉毘卖的侍女，拿着玉做的水器来井边打水，看见井水里映出了光，抬头一看，树上坐着一位英俊的男子，觉得十分奇怪。
title_en: The jewel in the vessel and the sea deity's daughter

summary_en: After three years Hoori remembered the past and heaved a great sigh.
summary_zh: 三年过去，火远理命想起往事，长长地叹了一口气。

summary_en: Later Toyotama-bime herself came out of the sea and said to Hoori: 'I am with child and my time has come.
summary_zh: 后来，丰玉毘卖亲自从海里出来，对火远理命说：我怀孕了，现在就要生了。
title_en: The birth-hut thatched with cormorant feathers

summary_en: As Ninigi was about to descend, at the heavenly eight-forked crossroads stood a deity whose light shone up to the Plain of High Heaven and down to the Central Land of Reed-Plains.
summary_zh: 迩迩艺命正要降临的时候，在天之八衢——天上八条道路交会的地方——站着一位神，他身上发出的光，向上照亮了高天原，向下照亮了苇原中国。

summary_en: Amaterasu assigned to Ninigi five attendant deities, the five chiefs of companies: Ame-no-koyane, Futo-tama, Ame-no-Uzume, Ishi-kori-dome and Tama-no-oya, all of whom had played their part before the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling.
summary_zh: 天照大神为迩迩艺命安排了五位随从的神，称为“五伴绪”：天儿屋命、布刀玉命、天宇受卖命、伊斯许理度卖命和玉祖命，他们都是当年在天之岩户前出过力的神。
title_en: The regalia and the five chiefs

summary_en: Ninigi left the heavenly rock-seat, pushed apart the eight-fold heavenly clouds, and with mighty way-dividing made his way down by the Floating Bridge of Heaven to the peak of Kuji-furu-take of Takachiho in Himuka in Tsukushi.
summary_zh: 迩迩艺命离开了天上的岩座，分开天上层层叠叠的八重云，威风凛凛地开出一条道路，经过天之浮桥，降落在筑紫日向的高千穗的久士布流多气峰上。

summary_en: Ninigi said to Ame-no-Uzume: 'Escort Sarutahiko, who served as our guide, back home.
summary_zh: 迩迩艺命对天宇受卖命说：你送那位为我们引路的猿田毘古神回去吧。
title_en: The Duchesses of Saru and the sea-slug

summary_en: At the cape of Kasasa, Ninigi met a beautiful maiden and asked whose daughter she was.
summary_zh: 迩迩艺命在笠沙的岬角遇见一位美丽的少女，问她是谁的女儿。
title_zh: 木花之佐久夜毘卖与石长比卖

summary_en: After some time Konohana-sakuya-hime came to Ninigi and said: 'I am with child and my time is near.
summary_zh: 过了些日子，木花之佐久夜毘卖来对迩迩艺命说：我怀孕了，就要生产了。

summary_en: Hoderi became the Luck of the Sea, catching fish broad of fin and narrow of fin with his hook; Hoori became the Luck of the Mountains, taking beasts rough of hair and soft of hair with his bow.
summary_zh: 火照命成了海幸彦，用鱼钩捕捞海里大大小小的鱼；火远理命成了山幸彦，用弓箭猎取山里大大小小的野兽。
title_en: The luck of the sea and the luck of the mountains

summary_en: As Hoori wept on the seashore, the salt deity Shio-tsuchi came and asked: 'Why do you weep, Sky's Sun-Height?' He told the story of the hook.
summary_zh: 火远理命在海边哭泣，这时盐椎神来了，问他：天津日高日子，你为什么哭？
title_en: The salt deity and the road to the sea palace

summary_en: The Heavenly Sovereign Keikō ruled from the palace of Hishiro at Makimuku.
summary_zh: 景行天皇在缠向的日代宫统治天下，他有许多儿子，其中有一对兄弟：哥哥叫大碓命，弟弟叫小碓命，也叫倭男具那命。

summary_en: From Kai Yamato Takeru crossed Shinano, subdued the deity of the Shinano pass, and came back to Owari, to Miyazu-hime's house, to keep his pledge.
summary_zh: 倭建命从甲斐越过科野，平定了科野坂的神，回到尾张，进了美夜受比卖的家，履行当初的约定。

summary_en: Coming down the mountain, he rested by the clear spring of Tamakurabe and his mind cleared a little, so the spring is called the Awakening Spring.
summary_zh: 倭建命下了山，来到玉仓部的清泉边休息，神志稍稍清醒了一些，所以那眼泉被叫作居寤清水。
title_en: Legs like a triple-bent rice cake

summary_en: At the moor of Nobo, longing for his home, he sang: Yamato is the best of lands; the green mountains fold round it like a fence; Yamato, how lovely.
summary_zh: 到了能烦野，倭建命思念故乡，唱道：大和是国中最好的地方，层层叠叠的青山像垣墙一样环绕，大和啊，多么美好。
title_en: The songs of home and the white bird

summary_en: The sovereign said: 'In the west there are two Kumaso bravoes who will not submit and have no respect.
summary_zh: 天皇说：西方有两个熊曾建，他们不肯归顺，没有礼数，你去把他们杀了。

summary_en: When the feast was at its height, Wo-usu drew the sword from his bosom, seized the elder Kumaso bravo by the collar and thrust the sword through his chest.
summary_zh: 宴会正热闹的时候，小碓命从怀里拔出短剑，抓住哥哥熊曾建的衣领，一剑刺穿了他的胸膛。

summary_en: On his way back Yamato Takeru subdued the deities of the mountains, the rivers and the straits, and then went into Izumo intending to kill the Izumo bravo.
summary_zh: 倭建命回京的路上，把山神、河神和海峡之神一一平定，然后进入出云国，想要杀死出云建。
title_en: The Izumo bravo and the wooden sword

summary_en: No sooner had Yamato Takeru returned than the sovereign commanded him again: 'Go and subdue the savage deities and unsubmissive people of the twelve roads of the East.' He sent with him Mi-suki-tomo-mimi-take-hiko, ancestor of the Kibi lords, and gave him a holly-wood spear eight fathoms long.
summary_zh: 倭建命刚刚回来，天皇又命令他说：你去把东方十二道那些凶暴的神和不肯归顺的人平定了。

summary_en: In Owari, Yamato Takeru entered the house of Miyazu-hime, ancestress of the rulers of Owari, and thought to marry her; then, deciding to marry her on his return, he pledged himself to her and went on east.
summary_zh: 倭建命到了尾张国，进了尾张国造的祖先美夜受比卖的家，本想娶她为妻，转念一想，等回来时再娶吧，就和她立下婚约，继续往东去了。
title_en: The fire on the moor of Sagamu

summary_en: From there Yamato Takeru crossed the sea of Hashirimizu.
summary_zh: 倭建命从那里出发，渡过走水海。

summary_en: Yamato Takeru went on deep into the East, subdued all the savage Emishi, pacified the savage deities of the mountains and rivers, and set out to return.
summary_zh: 倭建命继续深入东方，把凶暴的虾夷人都平定了，又平定了山河间凶暴的神，然后踏上了回程。
title_en: The white deer on the Ashigara pass

summary_en: Crossing from the pass into Kai, Yamato Takeru stayed at the palace of Sakaori.
summary_zh: 倭建命越过足柄坂，进入甲斐国，住在酒折宫里。

summary_en: Kay Kāvus inherited the throne of Iran and, seated in state with his champions around him and treasure heaped high, thought no one in the world more mighty than he.
summary_zh: 凯·卡乌斯继承了伊朗的王位，坐在宝座上，看着满朝的勇士和堆积如山的财宝，以为天下再也没有人比他更强大。

summary_en: Rostam came out of the cave with the White Demon's liver, the sunlight on his blood-soaked body; Olād, seeing him, took him for a demon and was terrified until he spoke.
summary_zh: 鲁斯塔姆带着白魔的肝走出洞穴，阳光照在他满是鲜血的身上，乌拉德看见他，吓得以为是魔鬼出来了，直到他开口说话才放下心来。

summary_en: Restored to strength, Kay Kāvus wrote to the king of Māzandarān commanding him to come and submit, surrender his treasure and become a vassal of Iran.
summary_zh: 凯·卡乌斯恢复了力量，写信给马赞德兰的国王，命令他前来投降，交出财宝，做伊朗的属国。
title_en: The king who became a rock

summary_en: But Kay Kāvus did not grow cautious from this lesson.
summary_zh: 可是凯·卡乌斯并没有因为这次教训变得谨慎。

summary_en: Zāl hastened to court and earnestly urged the king: 'Māzandarān is the land of demons; they bewitch men with magic.
summary_zh: 扎尔赶到宫中，恳切地劝国王：马赞德兰是魔鬼的国度，他们会用魔法迷惑人，以前的国王都不敢去，你不要拿伊朗的勇士和自己的性命去冒险。

summary_en: When Zāl received the letter he said to his son Rostam: 'The king is in peril, and only you can save him.
summary_zh: 扎尔收到信，对儿子鲁斯塔姆说：国王落难了，只有你能救他。

summary_en: The next day Rostam entered a scorching desert; the sun burned the earth like fire, and there was not a drop of water nor a patch of shade.
summary_zh: 第二天，鲁斯塔姆走进了一片炎热的沙漠，烈日像火一样烤着大地，四周没有一滴水，也没有一片树荫。

summary_en: That night Rostam slept by the spring, telling Rakhsh not to fight beasts alone again but to wake him at any danger.
summary_zh: 那天夜里，鲁斯塔姆睡在泉水边，叮嘱拉赫什：不要再自己去和野兽打斗，有危险就叫醒我。

summary_en: On the fourth day Rostam crossed a lovely valley to a spring, where beneath the trees rich carpets were spread with roast lamb, bread, fruit and a flask of wine, and a lute lay beside them.
summary_zh: 第四天，鲁斯塔姆穿过一片美丽的山谷，来到一眼泉水边，只见树荫下铺着华丽的毯子，摆满了烤好的羊肉、面包、水果和一瓶美酒，旁边还放着一把琴。

summary_en: On the fifth day Rostam entered a land of darkness without sun or moon, where he could not see his hand before him; he let Rakhsh find the way, and after a long time came out into the light, to green fields.
summary_zh: 第五天，鲁斯塔姆走进了一片没有日月、伸手不见五指的黑暗之地，他让拉赫什自己找路，走了很久，终于重见光明，来到一片绿油油的田野。

summary_en: Olād led Rostam on and told him: 'Ahead is the camp of the demon Arzhang, one of the chiefs of the demon host of Māzandarān, who guards the road to the king's prison; beyond it lie seven great mountains, and in a cave among them lives the White Demon with thousands of demons on guard.' Rostam tied Olād to a tree, waited for dawn, then rode alone on Rakhsh into Arzhang's camp with a roar like thunder that shook the demons' hearts.
summary_zh: 乌拉德带着鲁斯塔姆向前走，告诉他：前面是魔鬼阿尔章的营地，他是马赞德兰魔鬼军队的首领之一，守着通往国王监牢的道路；过了那里，再往前是七座大山，白魔就住在山中的一个洞穴里，他身边有成千上万的魔鬼守卫。

summary_en: Rostam found Kay Kāvus and the champions of Iran in their prison, all blind and suffering in darkness.
summary_zh: 鲁斯塔姆找到了被关押的凯·卡乌斯和伊朗的勇士们，他们都瞎了眼睛，在黑暗中受苦。

summary_en: One day, restless in heart, Rostam took his bow and lasso and rode Rakhsh to hunt on the border between Iran and Tūrān.
summary_zh: 有一天，鲁斯塔姆心中烦闷，就带上弓箭和套索，骑着拉赫什到伊朗与图兰交界的地方去打猎。

summary_en: On the second day, as soon as Sohrāb saw Rostam he came to meet him smiling: 'Did you sleep well?
summary_zh: 第二天，苏赫拉布一见到鲁斯塔姆，就笑着迎上去说：昨夜你睡得好吗？
title_en: The ruse of the second day

summary_en: Having escaped, Rostam went to a stream, washed himself, knelt and prayed to the Creator.
summary_zh: 鲁斯塔姆脱身以后，来到一条溪边，洗净了身体，跪在地上向造物主祈祷。

summary_en: At these words the world went dark before Rostam's eyes and he fell senseless.
summary_zh: 鲁斯塔姆听见这句话，眼前一黑，昏倒在地。

summary_en: The king of Samangān held a great feast for Rostam, and when he had drunk he was led to a chamber hung with brocade to rest.
summary_zh: 萨曼甘的国王为鲁斯塔姆举行了盛大的宴会，鲁斯塔姆喝了酒，被领到一间铺着锦缎的卧室里休息。

summary_en: Soon after the marriage Rakhsh was found, and Rostam had to return to Iran.
summary_zh: 婚后不久，人们找回了拉赫什，鲁斯塔姆必须回到伊朗去了。

summary_en: Sohrāb grew astonishingly fast: at one month he was like a child of a year, at three he rode and shot, at five he had a lion's courage, and at ten no one in Samangān could match him in arms.
summary_zh: 苏赫拉布长得出奇地快：一个月大时就像一岁的孩子，三岁时就学会了骑马射箭，五岁时有了狮子般的勇气，到了十岁，萨曼甘没有一个人能和他比武。

summary_en: Sohrāb chose himself a horse worthy of him and gathered an army.
summary_zh: 苏赫拉布为自己挑选了一匹配得上他的骏马，召集了一支军队。

summary_en: Sohrāb led his army into Iran and came to the White Castle on the border.
summary_zh: 苏赫拉布率领大军进入伊朗，来到边境上的白堡。
title_en: The warrior maiden of the White Castle

summary_en: When news of the White Castle's fall reached Kay Kāvus, the king was terrified and at once wrote to Rostam, sending the champion Gīv riding day and night to Zābulistān to beg him to come with all speed against the young enemy.
summary_zh: 白堡失守的消息传到凯·卡乌斯那里，国王惊恐万分，立刻写信给鲁斯塔姆，派勇士吉夫日夜兼程送到扎布尔斯坦，请他火速前来抵挡这个年轻的敌人。

summary_en: The Iranian army came before the White Castle and faced the Turanians across the plain.
summary_zh: 伊朗大军来到白堡前，与图兰军队隔着平原对阵。

summary_en: Sohrāb rode up before the Iranian host and shouted his challenge, then charged into the camp and cut down the banner before Kay Kāvus's tent, and not one Iranian champion dared come out.
summary_zh: 苏赫拉布骑马冲到伊朗军前，大声挑战，又冲进营中，砍倒了凯·卡乌斯帐前的旗帜，伊朗的勇士们没有一个敢出来应战。

summary_en: When King Manūchehr ruled Iran, Sām, lord of Zābulistān, was the bravest of his champions; he lacked nothing except a son.
summary_zh: 在马努切赫尔国王统治伊朗的时候，扎布尔斯坦的领主萨姆是国王最英勇的勇士，他什么都不缺，只盼望有一个儿子。

summary_en: With the king's consent Zāl rode day and night back to Zābulistān and on to Kābul.
summary_zh: 扎尔带着国王的许可，日夜兼程回到扎布尔斯坦，又赶往喀布尔。

summary_en: Soon Rūdābeh was with child.
summary_zh: 不久，鲁达贝怀了孕。
title_en: The hard labour and the Simorgh's feather

summary_en: Rostam grew so fast that ten nurses could not satisfy him, and once weaned he ate more than five grown men.
summary_zh: 鲁斯塔姆长得飞快，十个乳母都喂不饱他，断奶以后，他一个人吃的饭比五个大人还多。

summary_en: High on Mount Alborz lived a great bird called the Simorgh.
summary_zh: 厄尔布尔士山的高处，住着一只神鸟，名叫西摩格。

summary_en: One night Sām dreamed that a rider on an Arab horse came galloping from the direction of India and told him: 'Your son is alive.' He woke and told the priests his dream, asking what it meant.
summary_zh: 有一天夜里，萨姆梦见一个骑着阿拉伯骏马的人从印度方向疾驰而来，告诉他：你的儿子还活着。

summary_en: The Simorgh saw Sām below and knew he had come for his son.
summary_zh: 西摩格看见山下的萨姆，知道他是来找儿子的。
title_en: Zāl returns to the world of men

summary_en: Sent by the king to war, Sām left Zābulistān in Zāl's charge.
summary_zh: 萨姆奉国王之命出征，把扎布尔斯坦交给扎尔治理。

summary_en: Rūdābeh's maidens went out as if to gather roses by the river near Zāl's camp.
summary_zh: 鲁达贝的侍女们装作去采玫瑰，来到扎尔营地附近的河边。

summary_en: Zāl summoned the priests and wise men and told them his heart, but they were silent, for all knew Mehrāb descended from Zahhāk; how could a hero of Iran marry into the tyrant's line?
summary_zh: 扎尔召来祭司和贤者，把心事告诉了他们，他们都沉默不语，因为谁都知道梅赫拉布是佐哈克的后裔，伊朗的英雄怎能和暴君的子孙结亲？
title_en: The opposition of father and king

summary_en: When the news reached Kābul, Mehrāb learned for the first time of his daughter's love.
summary_zh: 消息传到喀布尔，梅赫拉布才知道女儿的事，他勃然大怒，拔出剑来要杀死鲁达贝，说她给全族带来了灭顶之灾。

summary_en: At Manūchehr's court the king had his wise men test Zāl with riddles.
summary_zh: 扎尔来到马努切赫尔的宫廷，国王让宫中的智者们用谜语来考验他。
title_en: The riddles of the wise men

summary_en: Wang Chong opens 'Lei Xu' thus: in high summer thunder and lightning come swift and fierce, splitting trees, wrecking houses and sometimes killing people.
summary_zh: 王充在《雷虚》的开头写道：盛夏的时候，雷电来得又快又猛，劈断树木，毁坏房屋，有时还会打死人。

summary_en: Wang first refutes the idea that thunder is Heaven's anger.
summary_zh: 王充首先反驳“雷是天怒”的说法。

summary_en: In 'Lei Xu' Wang returns again and again to one question: are the people and things struck by thunder chosen by Heaven, or simply in the way?
summary_zh: 王充在《雷虚》中反复回到同一个问题：雷击中的人和物，究竟是被上天特意选中的，还是偶然碰上的？

summary_en: Wang then describes how Han painters drew thunder: painters picture thunder as drums strung together one after another, like a chain of linked drums; and they draw a man with the look of a strongman, whom they call Leigong, the Thunder Lord, making him pull the linked drums with his left hand and raise a mallet in his right, as if striking.
summary_zh: 王充接着描述了汉代画工所画的雷的样子：画工们画雷的形状，是一面接一面串在一起的鼓，像一串连鼓；又画一个人，有着力士一样的容貌，称他为雷公，让他左手拉着连鼓，右手举着槌子，像是正在敲打的样子。

summary_en: Wang raises several objections to the painted Leigong.
summary_zh: 王充对画中的雷公提出了好几条质疑。

summary_en: Wang states his own view: thunder is fire.
summary_zh: 王充提出了自己的看法：雷，是火。

summary_en: Wang also uses an everyday experience to show thunder's force: pour a peck of water onto the fire of a smelting furnace, and the steam bursts and cracks with a sound like thunder; anyone too close will surely be scorched.
summary_zh: 王充又用一个日常的经验来说明雷的威力：拿一斗水浇进冶炼铸造的炉火里，水气激荡，迸裂开来，发出的声音就像雷一样；如果有人靠得太近，一定会被灼伤身体。

summary_en: In the conclusion of 'Lei Xu' Wang says: thunder is the surging energy of great yang.
summary_zh: 在《雷虚》的结论部分，王充说：雷是太阳之气激发出来的。
title_en: The surging energy of great yang

summary_en: The stela opens with the full titulary of Ramesses II: Horus, Mighty Bull, beautiful of crowns; King of Upper and Lower Egypt Usermaatre-Setepenre, Son of Re Ramesses-Meryamun, beloved of Amun-Re, lord of the gods of Thebes.
summary_zh: 石碑以拉美西斯二世的全套王衔开头：荷鲁斯，强壮的公牛，戴着美丽的王冠；上下埃及之王乌塞尔玛阿特拉-塞泰普恩拉，拉之子拉美西斯-美瑞阿蒙，受底比斯众神之主阿蒙-拉宠爱的人。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: While Khonsu-the-Provider and the spirit were speaking thus, the prince of Bakhtan stood by with his army in great fear.
summary_zh: 就在驱邪者孔苏和那个精灵这样交谈的时候，巴赫坦的王公和他的士兵们站在一旁，心里非常害怕。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: The prince of Bakhtan considered in his heart, saying: 'I will make this god stay here in Bakhtan; I will not let him go to Egypt.' So the god remained in Bakhtan three years and nine months.
summary_zh: 巴赫坦的王公在心里盘算着，说：我要让这位神留在巴赫坦，我不让他回埃及去。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: The prince of Bakhtan let the god go to Egypt and gave him very many gifts of every good thing, with many soldiers and horses.
summary_zh: 巴赫坦的王公让这位神启程回埃及，给了他许多各种各样的好东西作为礼物，还派了很多士兵和马匹护送。
uncertainty_note: 碑文中的年份与日期据现代学者的释读，不对应可考的史实。

summary_en: His Majesty was pleased with the princess of Bakhtan and took her as his wife, writing her name in the royal titulary as Great Royal Wife Neferure, 'the beauty of Re'.
summary_zh: 陛下很喜欢这位巴赫坦的公主，娶她为妻，在王衔中写下她的名字，称她为“伟大的王后奈芙鲁拉”，意思是“拉的美丽”。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: The stela goes on: in regnal year 23, second month of summer, day 22, His Majesty was in Thebes the Victorious, mistress of cities, performing the rites for his father Amun-Re, lord of the Thrones of the Two Lands, at his beautiful Feast of Southern Ipet, his favourite place since the beginning.
summary_zh: 碑文接着说：在陛下在位的第二十三年，夏季第二个月的第二十二天，陛下正在胜利之城底比斯——众城之主——为他的父亲阿蒙-拉，两地王座之主，举行南方伊佩特的美好节日，那是阿蒙从远古以来就最喜爱的地方。
title_en: The feast at Thebes and the messenger
uncertainty_note: 碑文中的年份与日期据现代学者的释读，不对应可考的史实。

summary_en: His Majesty said: 'Bring me the scribes of the House of Life and the officials of the residence.' They were brought to him at once.
summary_zh: 陛下说：把生命之屋的书吏和宫中的官员们带来。
title_en: The scribe of the House of Life
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: In regnal year 26, first month of summer, while His Majesty was again at Thebes celebrating the feast of Amun, the prince of Bakhtan sent another messenger before His Majesty, saying: 'O sovereign, my lord, may Your Majesty send a god to fight with this spirit.' This time the people of Bakhtan asked not for a learned man but for a god.
summary_zh: 到了陛下在位的第二十六年，夏季的第一个月，陛下又在底比斯为阿蒙举行节日的时候，巴赫坦的王公再一次派使者来到陛下面前，说：我的主人陛下，请陛下派一位神来，和这个精灵作战。
uncertainty_note: 碑文中的年份与日期据现代学者的释读，不对应可考的史实。

summary_en: His Majesty went before Khonsu-in-Thebes-Neferhotep and said: 'My good lord, I am once again before you on account of the daughter of the prince of Bakhtan.' Then Khonsu-in-Thebes-Neferhotep was carried to Khonsu-the-Provider, the great god who expels disease demons.
summary_zh: 陛下来到底比斯的孔苏·奈弗尔霍特普面前，说：我的好主人，我又一次来到您面前，是为了巴赫坦王公的女儿。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: His Majesty had Khonsu-the-Provider placed in a great bark, with five boats as escort, and chariots and many horses on the east and the west, to take the god to Bakhtan.
summary_zh: 陛下下令，让驱邪者孔苏登上一条大船，由五条小船护送，还配备了战车和许多马匹，从东到西护送着神前往巴赫坦。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: The god went to the place where Bentresh was and made the protection over the daughter of the prince of Bakhtan, and she was well at once.
summary_zh: 神来到本特蕾什所在的地方，为巴赫坦王公的女儿施行了护佑。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: Then the spirit that was with her said before Khonsu-the-Provider: 'Welcome in peace, great god who expels disease demons!
summary_zh: 那个附在公主身上的精灵，当着驱邪者孔苏的面说：欢迎你平安到来，驱赶病魔的伟大的神！
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: The first scene shows Amun-Re, king of the gods, enthroned before the gods of Thebes and Heliopolis.
summary_zh: 浮雕的第一幕画的是众神之王阿蒙-拉坐在宝座上，面前是底比斯和赫利奥波利斯的众神。

summary_en: After the birth the goddess Hathor carried the child to Amun.
summary_zh: 孩子出生以后，女神哈托尔把她抱到阿蒙面前。

summary_en: Next Amun commands the goddesses to nurse the child.
summary_zh: 接下来，阿蒙吩咐众女神哺育这个孩子。

summary_en: In the last scenes of the cycle Thoth presents the child and her ka together to Amun (Brunner's scene 14).
summary_zh: 在诞生浮雕的最后几幕，托特把孩子和她的卡一起呈到阿蒙面前（学者布鲁纳编为第十四幕）。
title_en: Thoth presents the child, and the gods fix her lifetime

summary_en: In the next scene Amun speaks with Thoth, god of wisdom, scribe and messenger of the gods, shown with the head of an ibis.
summary_zh: 下一幕里，阿蒙与智慧之神托特交谈。

summary_en: The third scene shows Thoth leading the way and Amun following, going together to the palace where Queen Ahmose is.
summary_zh: 第三幕画的是托特在前面领路，阿蒙跟在后面，一起前往王后雅赫摩斯所在的王宫。

summary_en: Amun came to Ahmose's chamber in the form of her husband, Thutmose I.
summary_zh: 阿蒙化作王后的丈夫图特摩斯一世的模样，来到雅赫摩斯的寝宫。

summary_en: Leaving the queen, Amun came to Khnum, the potter god, and commanded him to fashion the child to be born.
summary_zh: 阿蒙离开王后以后，来到陶工之神克努姆面前，吩咐他塑造将要出生的孩子。

summary_en: This is one of the most famous scenes of the cycle: ram-headed Khnum sits at his potter's wheel, on which stand two identical small children — Hatshepsut's body and her ka.
summary_zh: 这一幕是整组浮雕中最著名的画面之一：羊头的克努姆坐在陶轮前，陶轮上站着两个一模一样的小孩，一个是哈特谢普苏特的身体，一个是她的卡。
title_en: The child on the potter's wheel

summary_en: When the child had been shaped on the wheel, Thoth appeared again — this time before Queen Ahmose, to announce the birth to her.
summary_zh: 孩子在陶轮上塑造完成以后，托特又一次出场。

summary_en: Next Khnum and Heqet, one on each side, take Queen Ahmose by the hands and lead her to the birth chamber.
summary_zh: 接下来，克努姆和赫凯特一左一右，牵着王后雅赫摩斯的手，领她走向产房。

summary_en: The birth scene is solemn and crowded: Queen Ahmose sits enthroned holding the newborn child, surrounded by many gods and spirits in rows, some kneeling, some raising their hands in acclaim.
summary_zh: 诞生的一幕画得庄严而拥挤：王后雅赫摩斯坐在宝座上，抱着刚出生的婴儿，四周围绕着许多神灵和精灵，它们分成几排，有的跪着，有的举着手表示欢呼。
uncertainty_note: 诞生一幕残缺较多，部分神灵的身份学者意见不一。

summary_en: The papyrus begins: once there were two brothers of one mother and one father.
summary_zh: 纸草一开头说：从前有两个兄弟，同一个母亲、同一个父亲所生。

summary_en: Bata loved her very much.
summary_zh: 巴塔深深地爱着她。
title_en: The sea and a lock of hair

summary_en: Pharaoh summoned the learned scribes, who said to him: 'This lock of hair belongs to a daughter of Pre-Harakhti, in whom is the fluid of every god; it is a greeting to you from another land.
summary_zh: 法老召来了精通学问的书吏，他们对法老说：这缕头发属于拉-哈拉赫提的一个女儿，所有神的精华都在她身上，这是从另一个国度给您的礼物。

summary_en: Pharaoh asked her about her husband, and she said to Pharaoh: 'Let the pine be felled and cut to pieces.' So Pharaoh sent soldiers with their tools to fell the pine.
summary_zh: 法老问她关于她丈夫的事，她对法老说：让人去砍倒那棵松树，把它砍成碎片。

summary_en: On the day after the pine was felled, Anubis, Bata's elder brother, entered his house and sat down to wash his hands; he was given a jug of beer, and it fermented; he was given another of wine, and it turned bad.
summary_zh: 就在松树被砍倒的第二天，巴塔的哥哥阿努比斯走进家里，坐下洗手，有人递给他一罐啤酒，啤酒起了泡沫；又递给他一罐葡萄酒，葡萄酒也变浑浊了。

summary_en: Bata said to his elder brother: 'See, I shall become a great bull of every beautiful colour, whose nature no one will know.
summary_zh: 巴塔对哥哥说：看，我要变成一头公牛，身上有各种美丽的颜色，没有人知道它的来历。

summary_en: When the bull was slaughtered, two drops of its blood fell beside the two doorposts of Pharaoh's palace and grew into two great persea trees, each of them very beautiful.
summary_zh: 公牛被宰杀时，它的两滴血落在法老宫殿门口的两根门柱旁，长成了两棵高大的鳄梨树，每一棵都美极了。
title_en: The persea trees and the new king

summary_en: Every morning Bata drove the cattle out and every evening brought them back, laden with all the vegetables of the field, with milk, with wood and with every good thing of the field, and laid them before his elder brother; when Anubis and his wife had eaten and drunk, Bata went to the stable and slept among his cattle.
summary_zh: 每天早晨，巴塔赶着牛群出去，晚上再把它们赶回来，背上背着田里的各种蔬菜、牛奶、木柴和一切好东西，放在哥哥面前，哥哥和嫂子吃喝完毕，他才回到牛棚里，和牛群睡在一起。

summary_en: At ploughing time the brothers went together to plough.
summary_zh: 到了耕种的季节，兄弟俩一起到田里去犁地。

summary_en: When Bata had gone, his brother's wife was afraid of what she had said.
summary_zh: 巴塔走后，嫂子害怕自己说的话被传出去。

summary_en: Hearing this, the elder brother became like an Upper Egyptian leopard.
summary_zh: 哥哥一听，就像上埃及的豹子一样暴怒。

summary_en: As he fled, Bata prayed to Pre-Harakhti, saying: 'My good lord, it is you who judge the wrongdoer from the just.' And Re heard all his plea.
summary_zh: 巴塔一边逃跑，一边向太阳神拉-哈拉赫提祈祷，说：我的好主人，您是分辨恶人和义人的神。

summary_en: When the land grew light and the sun rose, the brothers looked at each other across the water.
summary_zh: 天亮了，太阳升起来，两兄弟隔着河相望。

summary_en: Bata said to his elder brother: 'You remember one bad thing; can you not remember one good thing, or a thing I did for you?
summary_zh: 巴塔对哥哥说：你只记得坏事，就不能记得一件好事，或者我为你做过的一件事吗？
title_en: The heart in the Valley of the Pine

summary_en: Bata lived alone in the Valley of the Pine, hunting desert game by day and coming back at evening to sleep under the pine on whose flower his heart lay.
summary_zh: 巴塔在松树谷里独自生活，白天打猎，晚上回到松树下睡觉，他的心就放在松树的花顶上。

summary_en: The two horizontal lines at the top of the slab give King Shabaka's titles and a statement: the King of Upper and Lower Egypt Shabaka, beloved of Ptah-South-of-his-Wall, living like Re for ever.
summary_zh: 石板最上面的两行横写的文字，是沙巴卡国王的王衔和一段说明：上下埃及之王沙巴卡，受“城墙之南的普塔”喜爱的人，愿他像拉一样永远活着。

summary_en: The text says: so it is said of Ptah, 'He who made all and created the gods.' He is Ta-tenen, who gave birth to the gods, and from whom every thing came forth — foods, provisions, divine offerings, all good things.
summary_zh: 碑文说：所以人们说普塔是“创造一切、生出众神的那一位”。

summary_en: The text goes on: he gave birth to the gods, he made the towns, he established the nomes, he placed the gods in their shrines, he settled their offerings, he established their shrines, he made their bodies according to their wishes.
summary_zh: 碑文接着说：他生出了众神，他建造了城市，他设立了各州，他把众神安置在他们的神龛里，他确定了他们的祭品，他建立了他们的神殿，他按照他们的心愿做出了他们的身体。

summary_en: The last part of the text returns to Osiris.
summary_zh: 碑文的最后一部分回到了奥西里斯的故事。

summary_en: After the preface the text praises Ptah: the King of Upper and Lower Egypt is this Great Name, Ta-tenen, South-of-his-Wall, Lord of Eternity.
summary_zh: 序言之后，碑文称颂普塔：上下埃及之王就是这个伟大的名字——塔特恩，城墙之南，永恒之主。

summary_en: Next the text tells a story of kingship.
summary_zh: 碑文接着讲了一个关于王权的故事。

summary_en: But then it seemed wrong to Geb that the portion of Horus was like the portion of Seth.
summary_zh: 可是后来，盖布觉得荷鲁斯的份额和塞特的份额一样，这样不对。

summary_en: The text goes on: reed and papyrus were placed on the double door of the house of Ptah.
summary_zh: 碑文接着说：芦苇和纸草被放在普塔神庙的双扇大门上。
uncertainty_note: 此段之后石板有大段文字因被用作磨盘而磨损，残缺处不补写。

summary_en: After the worn section the text enters its most famous part, the 'theology'.
summary_zh: 在磨损的部分之后，碑文进入了最著名的“神学”部分。

summary_en: The text goes on: there took shape in the heart, there took shape on the tongue the form of Atum.
summary_zh: 碑文接着说：在心中成形的，在舌上成形的，是阿图姆的形象。

summary_en: The text then compares Ptah's Ennead with Atum's: his Ennead is before him as heart and tongue, teeth and lips.
summary_zh: 碑文接着把普塔的九柱神和阿图姆的九柱神作了对比：普塔的九柱神在他面前，是心与舌、牙齿与嘴唇。

summary_en: The text then explains how this creation works: the sight of the eyes, the hearing of the ears, the breathing of the nose report to the heart.
summary_zh: 碑文接着解释这种创造是怎样发生的：眼睛的看见，耳朵的听见，鼻子的呼吸，都报告给心。
title_en: What the heart devises and the tongue commands

summary_en: The poet begins by saying he will sing of Apollo who shoots from afar, before whom the gods tremble when he enters the house of Zeus: they all rise from their seats, and only Leto his mother stays seated beside Zeus.
summary_zh: 诗人一开头就说，他要歌颂远射之神阿波罗，因为当阿波罗走进宙斯的宫殿时，众神都在他面前发抖，纷纷从座位上站起来，只有母亲勒托还安坐在宙斯身边。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: Apollo came to the city of the Phlegyae and up the snowy slopes below Parnassus to Crisa, a shoulder of the hill turned westward, with a great cliff hanging over it and a hollow, rugged glen below.
summary_zh: 阿波罗来到佛勒古埃斯人的城市，又走上帕尔纳索斯山下积雪的山坡，来到克里萨。
title_en: The foundations and the dragon at the spring
title_zh: 神庙的地基与泉边的母龙
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: Here the poet tells an older story.
summary_zh: 诗人在这里插进了一段旧事。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: Whoever met the she-dragon, the day of doom swept him away, until far-shooting Apollo let fly a strong arrow at her.
summary_zh: 凡是遇上这条母龙的人，末日都会到来，直到远射之神阿波罗向她射出一支强劲的箭。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: When the temple was built, Phoebus Apollo pondered what men he should bring to be his ministers in rocky Pytho.
summary_zh: 神庙建好了，福玻斯·阿波罗开始考虑，该找什么样的人来在多岩的皮托做他的祭司，为他主持祭祀。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: When the ship came to shore, far-shooting Apollo leapt from it like a star at midday, sparks flying from him and the brightness reaching to heaven.
summary_zh: 船靠了岸，远射之神阿波罗像一颗正午的星星一样从船上跃出，火花四溅，光芒直冲天际。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: Carrying the far-shooting god, Leto went through the lands and islands of Greece looking for a place that would let her give birth.
summary_zh: 勒托怀着远射之神，走遍了希腊的土地和岛屿，想找一个肯让她生产的地方。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: Leto came to Delos and said to the island: 'Delos, would you be the home of my son Phoebus Apollo and let him build a rich temple on you?
summary_zh: 勒托来到得洛斯，对这座小岛说：得洛斯啊，你愿意做我儿子福玻斯·阿波罗的家，在你这里为他建一座丰盛的神庙吗？
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: On Delos Leto was racked with labour for nine days and nine nights.
summary_zh: 勒托在得洛斯开始了阵痛，一连九天九夜，痛苦难当。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: As soon as Eileithyia set foot on Delos, the pains took hold of Leto and she was ready to give birth.
summary_zh: 厄勒梯亚一踏上得洛斯，阵痛就攫住了勒托，她就要生了。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: As soon as Phoebus had tasted ambrosia, the golden swaddling bands could no longer hold him, nor could the cords restrain him; all the bands fell loose.
summary_zh: 福玻斯一尝到神食，金色的襁褓就再也包不住他了，身上的带子也束不住他，所有的布条都松开了。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: The poet describes the gathering on Delos: the long-robed Ionians come together with their children and wives to honour Apollo, delighting him with boxing, dancing and song.
summary_zh: 诗人描写了得洛斯的盛会：穿着长袍的伊奥尼亚人带着妻儿聚集到岛上来纪念阿波罗，用拳击、舞蹈和歌唱来取悦他。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: The second part of the hymn changes scene.
summary_zh: 颂歌的第二部分换了一个场景。
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: Again the poet asks how he should sing of the god, and chooses to tell how Apollo sought a place to found an oracle for men.
summary_zh: 诗人又问：我该怎样歌颂你呢？
uncertainty_note: 坐标只引用实体档案，不为单个情节推断位置。

summary_en: The poet asks the Muse to sing of Hermes, son of Zeus and Maia, lord of Cyllene and of Arcadia rich in flocks, swift messenger of the gods.
summary_zh: 诗人请缪斯歌唱赫尔墨斯，宙斯和迈亚的儿子，库勒涅山和牛羊成群的阿卡狄亚的主人，众神迅捷的使者。

summary_en: The two came to the summit of fragrant Olympus, to their father Zeus, where the scales of judgement were set.
summary_zh: 两位神来到芬芳的奥林波斯山顶，来到父亲宙斯面前，正义的天平就摆在那里。

summary_en: The brothers came to the byre by the Alpheus, and Hermes drove the cattle out of the rocky cave.
summary_zh: 两兄弟来到阿尔甫斯河边的牛棚，赫尔墨斯把牛从石洞里赶了出来。

summary_en: The brothers drove the cattle back to the holy meadow and returned to snowy Olympus, and Zeus was glad to see them reconciled.
summary_zh: 两兄弟赶着牛群回到神圣的草地，然后回到积雪的奥林波斯山，宙斯看见他们和好，心里很高兴。

summary_en: As soon as Hermes leapt from his mother's immortal womb he would not lie still in his holy cradle, but sprang over the threshold of the high-roofed cave to look for Apollo's cattle.
summary_zh: 赫尔墨斯从母亲不朽的怀里一跳下来，就不肯安安静静地躺在神圣的摇篮里，跨过高高的门槛，去找阿波罗的牛群。

summary_en: But Hermes had other things in mind.
summary_zh: 可是赫尔墨斯心里想的是别的事。

summary_en: As Hermes drove the cattle across the plain past flowery Onchestus, an old man tending his vineyard saw the child driving them.
summary_zh: 赫尔墨斯赶着牛穿过平原，经过鲜花盛开的昂刻斯托斯时，一个老人正在葡萄园里劳作，看见了这个赶牛的孩子。

summary_en: At the Alpheus Hermes gathered a pile of wood and began to seek the art of fire.
summary_zh: 到了阿尔甫斯河边，赫尔墨斯捡来许多木柴，开始想办法生火。

summary_en: Before dawn Hermes came back to the bright peaks of Cyllene.
summary_zh: 天亮以前，赫尔墨斯回到了库勒涅山的高峰。

summary_en: Dawn rose from deep-flowing Ocean bringing light to men, and Apollo came to holy Onchestus, where he found the old man tending the hedge of his vineyard by the road.
summary_zh: 黎明从大洋深处升起，给人们带来光明。

summary_en: Apollo came to the wooded mountain of Cyllene, to the deep cave in the rock where the deathless nymph Maia had borne the child of Zeus.
summary_zh: 阿波罗来到库勒涅山林木茂盛的山上，来到岩石中幽深的山洞，那是不死的仙女迈亚生下宙斯之子的地方。

summary_en: As he spoke, Hermes kept glancing about with twinkling eyes, his brows going up and down, and gave a long whistle, as if listening to an idle tale.
summary_zh: 赫尔墨斯一边说，一边眼睛不停地眨着，眉毛扬来扬去，四处张望，吹着长长的口哨，像在听一个无聊的故事。

summary_en: The poet asks the Muse to tell of golden Aphrodite, the Cyprian, who stirs sweet desire in the gods and subdues the tribes of mortal men, the birds that fly in the air and all the creatures of dry land and sea: all of them care for her works.
summary_zh: 诗人请缪斯歌唱金色的阿佛洛狄忒，塞浦路斯的女神。
title_zh: 阿佛洛狄忒的力量与雅典娜

summary_en: Aphrodite, daughter of Zeus, answered: 'Anchises, most glorious of mortal men, take courage and do not fear too much.
summary_zh: 宙斯的女儿阿佛洛狄忒回答说：安喀塞斯，凡人中最光荣的人，鼓起勇气，不要太害怕。
title_zh: 埃涅阿斯与伽倪墨得斯

summary_en: Aphrodite told of another Trojan.
summary_zh: 阿佛洛狄忒又讲了另一个特洛伊人的故事。

summary_en: Aphrodite said: 'If you could live on as you are now in looks and form, and be called my husband, sorrow would not enfold my heart.
summary_zh: 阿佛洛狄忒说：如果你能保持现在的容貌和身材活下去，被称为我的丈夫，悲伤就不会笼罩我的心。

summary_en: The second is Artemis of the golden arrows and the loud hunting cry, whom laughter-loving Aphrodite never tames in love.
summary_zh: 第二位是戴着金冠、喜爱喧闹的狩猎女神阿耳忒弥斯，爱笑的阿佛洛狄忒从来不能用爱情制服她。

summary_en: The third is the revered maiden Hestia, whom Aphrodite's works do not please either.
summary_zh: 第三位是可敬的处女赫斯提亚，阿佛洛狄忒的事业同样不能让她高兴。

summary_en: Apart from these three, there is nothing among the blessed gods or mortal men that has escaped Aphrodite.
summary_zh: 除了这三位，无论是有福的神还是会死的人，没有谁能躲开阿佛洛狄忒。

summary_en: When laughter-loving Aphrodite saw Anchises she loved him, and desire seized her heart.
summary_zh: 爱笑的阿佛洛狄忒一看见安喀塞斯，就爱上了他，强烈的渴望攫住了她的心。

summary_en: She found Anchises left alone at the huts, with beauty given by the gods.
summary_zh: 她发现安喀塞斯独自一人留在小屋里，他有着众神赐予的美貌。

summary_en: Aphrodite, daughter of Zeus, answered: 'Anchises, most glorious of earth-born men, I am no goddess; why do you liken me to the deathless ones?
summary_zh: 宙斯的女儿阿佛洛狄忒回答说：安喀塞斯，你是地上的人中最光荣的，我不是女神，你为什么把我比作不死的神？

summary_en: So speaking, the goddess put sweet desire in Anchises' heart.
summary_zh: 女神说着，把甜蜜的渴望放进了安喀塞斯的心里。

summary_en: Clothed again, the goddess stood in the hut, her head reaching to the well-hewn roof-beam, and from her cheeks shone unearthly beauty such as belongs to rich-crowned Cytherea.
summary_zh: 女神穿好衣服，站在小屋里，头几乎碰到精工建造的屋顶，脸颊上闪耀着不朽的美，那是戴着美丽花冠的库忒瑞亚才有的美。

summary_en: Book Five of the Iliad is Diomedes' great day, and the book in which Ares appears most.
summary_zh: 《伊利亚特》第五卷是狄俄墨得斯大显身手的一卷，也是阿瑞斯在全诗中出场最多的一卷。

summary_en: In Book Thirteen the Trojan Deiphobus hurled his spear at Idomeneus and missed, but struck Ascalaphus, son of Ares, through the shoulder, and he fell in the dust clutching the earth.
summary_zh: 第十三卷里，特洛伊人得伊福玻斯向伊多墨纽斯投出长矛，没有投中，却刺中了阿瑞斯的儿子阿斯卡拉福斯的肩膀，阿斯卡拉福斯倒在尘土里，双手抓地而死。

summary_en: At the opening of Book Twenty, as Achilles returns to battle, Zeus calls the gods together and tells them they may help whichever side they please, lest Achilles overstep fate and take Troy before its time.
summary_zh: 第二十卷开头，阿喀琉斯重返战场，宙斯召集众神，宣布他们可以随意帮助自己喜欢的一方，免得阿喀琉斯违背命运，提前攻下特洛伊城。

summary_en: In Book Twenty-One the gods come to blows.
summary_zh: 到了第二十一卷，众神真的动起手来。

summary_en: Aphrodite, daughter of Zeus, took Ares by the hand and led him away, groaning continually and scarcely able to get his breath.
summary_zh: 宙斯的女儿阿佛洛狄忒拉住阿瑞斯的手，把不停呻吟、好不容易才缓过气来的他扶离战场。

summary_en: On the field Diomedes, fired by Athena, carries all before him, and he even wounds Aphrodite in the wrist when she comes to rescue her wounded son Aeneas.
summary_zh: 战场上，狄俄墨得斯在雅典娜的鼓舞下所向无敌，连阿佛洛狄忒也被他刺伤了手腕——她是来救自己受伤的儿子埃涅阿斯的。

summary_en: Aphrodite returns to Olympus and falls on the knees of her mother Dione, who takes her in her arms and comforts her: 'Bear it, my child; many of us who dwell on Olympus have suffered at the hands of men, and we bring hard pains on one another.' Then she gives examples, and the first is Ares: the two sons of Aloeus, mighty Otus and Ephialtes, bound Ares in strong chains and kept him in a bronze jar for thirteen months.
summary_zh: 阿佛洛狄忒回到奥林波斯，扑倒在母亲狄俄涅的膝上。
title_en: Thirteen months in a bronze jar

summary_en: Three times Diomedes sprang at Aeneas, whom Apollo was shielding; the fourth time Apollo shouted at him: 'Son of Tydeus, give way, and do not think to match yourself with the gods.' Apollo carried Aeneas to his temple in Pergamus to be healed, and then said to Ares: 'Ares, Ares, bane of men, bloodstained stormer of cities, will you not go and drive this man from the field — the son of Tydeus, who would now fight even father Zeus?
summary_zh: 狄俄墨得斯一连三次冲向被阿波罗保护着的埃涅阿斯，第四次冲上去时，阿波罗厉声喝退了他：提丢斯的儿子，退回去，不要妄想和神平起平坐。

summary_en: Hector sprang from his chariot and went about among the host brandishing his two spears, rousing them to fight, and the Trojans turned and faced the Achaeans.
summary_zh: 赫克托耳从战车上跳下来，挥舞着两支长矛，在整个队伍中奔走，激起可怕的战斗。

summary_en: Before Ares and Hector the Achaeans neither fled to their ships nor charged, but gave ground step by step, for they knew Ares was among the Trojans.
summary_zh: 希腊人在阿瑞斯和赫克托耳面前既没有逃回船边，也没有挺身迎战，而是一步步地后退，因为他们知道阿瑞斯在特洛伊人中间。

summary_en: White-armed Hera, seeing the Achaeans perish in the fierce fighting, said to Athena: 'Alas, child of aegis-bearing Zeus, we promised Menelaus that he would sack Troy and return home safe; that promise is vain if we let Ares rage like this.
summary_zh: 白臂的赫拉看见希腊人在激战中纷纷倒下，就对雅典娜说：真是糟糕，持埃癸斯盾的宙斯的孩子，我们曾向墨涅拉俄斯许诺，他一定会攻下特洛伊城平安回家，如果我们任由阿瑞斯这样发狂，这个诺言就落空了。

summary_en: Athena found Diomedes cooling his wound and taunted him for being less bold than his father Tydeus.
summary_zh: 雅典娜找到正在擦拭伤口的狄俄墨得斯，责备他不如父亲提丢斯勇敢。

summary_en: Ares came swiftly to Olympus, home of the gods, sat down in pain beside Zeus, showed him the immortal blood flowing from his wound and complained: 'Father Zeus, are you not angry at such violence?
summary_zh: 阿瑞斯飞快地来到众神居住的奥林波斯，满心痛苦地坐在宙斯身边，让父亲看他伤口里流出的神血，诉苦说：父亲宙斯，看到这种暴行你不生气吗？

summary_en: Cadmus the Phoenician founded Thebes and married Harmonia, daughter of Ares and Aphrodite, who bore him daughters, Autonoe, Ino, Semele and Agave, and a son, Polydorus.
summary_zh: 腓尼基人卡德摩斯建立了忒拜，娶了阿瑞斯和阿佛洛狄忒的女儿哈耳摩尼亚，生下了女儿奥托诺厄、伊诺、塞墨勒和阿高厄，还有儿子波吕多罗斯。

summary_en: Wishing to be ferried from Icaria to Naxos, Dionysus hired a pirate ship of Tyrrhenians.
summary_zh: 狄俄倪索斯想从伊卡里亚岛渡海到纳克索斯岛，就雇了一条第勒尼安海盗的船。

summary_en: The Library closes Dionysus's wanderings on earth in one sentence: men learned that he was a god and honoured him; and having brought up his mother from Hades and named her Thyone, he ascended with her to heaven.
summary_zh: 《书库》用一句话为狄俄倪索斯在大地上的游历作了结尾：人们知道了他是神，开始崇拜他；他从冥府带回了自己的母亲，给她取名堤俄涅，和她一起升上了天空。
title_en: Bringing his mother up from Hades

summary_en: Telling of the kings of Athens, the Library mentions Dionysus again.
summary_zh: 《书库》在讲雅典诸王的时候，又提到了狄俄倪索斯。

summary_en: Unable to refuse, Zeus came to her bridal chamber in a chariot with lightnings and thunderings and launched a thunderbolt.
summary_zh: 宙斯无法拒绝，只好驾着战车，带着闪电和雷鸣来到塞墨勒的屋子，掷出了一道雷电。

summary_en: After Semele's death the other daughters of Cadmus spread the report that she had lain with a mortal man and falsely accused Zeus, and that she was blasted by the thunderbolt for it.
summary_zh: 塞墨勒死后，卡德摩斯的其他女儿们四处散布流言，说塞墨勒是和一个凡人同床，却谎称是宙斯，所以才被雷电击死。

summary_en: But Hera found out, and in her anger drove Ino and Athamas mad.
summary_zh: 可是赫拉还是知道了。
title_en: The madness of Ino and Athamas
title_zh: 伊诺与阿塔玛斯的疯狂

summary_en: To keep him from Hera, Zeus turned Dionysus into a kid, and Hermes took him to the nymphs who dwelt at Nysa in Asia.
summary_zh: 为了不让赫拉再找到他，宙斯把狄俄倪索斯变成了一只小山羊。

summary_en: The third book goes on: Dionysus discovered the vine.
summary_zh: 《书库》第三卷接着说：狄俄倪索斯是葡萄的发现者。

summary_en: In Thrace, Lycurgus son of Dryas, king of the Edonians who dwell beside the river Strymon, was the first to insult and expel Dionysus.
summary_zh: 在色雷斯，斯特律蒙河边的厄多涅斯人的国王、德律阿斯的儿子吕枯耳戈斯第一个侮辱了狄俄倪索斯，把他赶了出去。

summary_en: Having traversed Thrace and the whole of India and set up pillars there, Dionysus came to Thebes.
summary_zh: 狄俄倪索斯穿过色雷斯和整个印度，在那里竖起了石柱，然后来到了忒拜。

summary_en: To stop the rites Pentheus went to Cithaeron to spy on the raving women.
summary_zh: 彭透斯想阻止酒神的仪式，就来到喀泰戎山上，暗中窥探那些狂欢的女人。

summary_en: Telling of the Titans' children, the Library says that Asteria, daughter of Coeus, fled Zeus in the likeness of a quail and flung herself into the sea, and a city was called Asteria after her and later Delos.
summary_zh: 《书库》在讲提坦的子女时说，科俄斯的女儿阿斯忒里亚为了躲避宙斯，化作一只鹌鹑跳进大海，那座城市先是叫阿斯忒里亚，后来叫得洛斯。

summary_en: Recounting the Arcadian line, the Library tells of Callisto.
summary_zh: 《书库》讲阿卡狄亚的谱系时，提到了卡利斯托。

summary_en: The Epitome of the Library tells of the Trojan War.
summary_zh: 《书库》的《摘要》部分讲特洛伊战争。

summary_en: On receiving the oracle Agamemnon sent Odysseus and the herald Talthybius to Clytemnestra to ask for Iphigenia, pretending he had promised to give her to Achilles to wife as a reward for his service.
summary_zh: 阿伽门农接到神谕后，派奥德修斯和传令官塔尔堤比俄斯去见妻子克吕泰涅斯特拉，向她要伊菲革涅亚，假说他答应把女儿嫁给阿喀琉斯，作为对阿喀琉斯参战的酬谢。

summary_en: In the same section the Library tells how the twins avenged their mother.
summary_zh: 同一节里，《书库》讲了一件姐弟俩为母亲报仇的事。

summary_en: The Library says: Artemis slew Orion in Delos.
summary_zh: 《书库》说：阿耳忒弥斯在得洛斯杀死了俄里翁。

summary_en: In its first book the Library also tells of two giant brothers, Otus and Ephialtes, called the Aloadae — nominally sons of Aloeus, but in truth sons of Poseidon.
summary_zh: 《书库》第一卷还讲了一对巨人兄弟，俄托斯和厄菲阿尔忒斯，人称阿洛伊代兄弟。

summary_en: Oeneus, king of Calydon in Aetolia, offering the first-fruits of the year's crops to all the gods, forgot Artemis alone.
summary_zh: 埃托利亚的卡吕冬国王俄纽斯在一年的收成之后，把最早的果实献给所有的神，唯独忘了阿耳忒弥斯。

summary_en: Admetus, king of Pherae, wooed Alcestis, daughter of Pelias.
summary_zh: 斐赖国王阿德墨托斯向珀利阿斯的女儿阿尔刻提斯求婚。

summary_en: The Library's second book tells the labours of Heracles.
summary_zh: 《书库》第二卷讲赫拉克勒斯的十二项任务。

summary_en: The Library's third book tells the stories of Thebes.
summary_zh: 《书库》第三卷讲忒拜的故事。

summary_en: Amphion, king of Thebes, married Niobe, daughter of Tantalus, who bore seven sons and seven daughters — the Library notes that Hesiod gives ten of each and Homer six of each.
summary_zh: 忒拜王安菲翁娶了坦塔罗斯的女儿尼俄柏，生了七个儿子和七个女儿——《书库》还注明，赫西俄德说他们有十个儿子十个女儿，荷马说有六个儿子六个女儿。

summary_en: Hesiod says that first of all Chaos came to be, and next wide-bosomed Earth, the ever-sure foundation of all the deathless ones who hold the peaks of snowy Olympus; and dim Tartarus in the depth of the wide-pathed Earth; and Eros, fairest among the deathless gods, who unnerves the limbs and overcomes the mind and wise counsels of all gods and men.
summary_zh: 赫西俄德说，最先出现的是混沌卡俄斯，接着是宽胸的大地盖亚，她是住在积雪的奥林波斯山顶上的众神永远稳固的根基；然后是道路宽阔的大地深处幽暗的塔耳塔罗斯；还有爱神厄洛斯，不死的神中最美的一位，他能松弛四肢，征服所有神和人的心智与谋划。

summary_en: The poet then tells why Styx has such honour.
summary_zh: 诗人接着讲斯梯克斯为什么享有这样的荣誉。

summary_en: Phoebe came to the desired bed of Coeus, and the goddess, conceiving in the love of the god, bore dark-gowned Leto.
summary_zh: 提坦福柏来到科俄斯的爱床，女神在男神的爱中怀孕，生下了穿着深色长袍的勒托。

summary_en: Asteria conceived and bore Hecate, and the poet praises her at length: Zeus the son of Cronos honoured her above all and gave her splendid gifts, a share of the earth and the unfruitful sea, and honour in starry heaven, and she is honoured most of all by the deathless gods.
summary_zh: 阿斯忒里亚怀了孕，生下了赫卡忒。

summary_en: After describing how Zeus overcame the Titans and shut them in Tartarus, the poet leads his hearers to the edge of the world.
summary_zh: 在描写宙斯战胜提坦、把他们关进塔耳塔罗斯之后，诗人带领听众来到世界的边缘。
title_en: The threshold of Night and Day

summary_en: There too the children of dark Night have their dwellings, Sleep and Death, awful gods.
summary_zh: 就在那里，幽暗黑夜的孩子们也有自己的住所：睡眠和死亡，两位可怕的神。
title_en: The house of Sleep and Death

summary_en: Near the end of the Theogony the poet lists the children goddesses bore to mortal men.
summary_zh: 《神谱》快结束时，诗人列出了女神与凡间男子所生的孩子。

summary_en: Next, the Theogony says, Night conceived in love with Erebus and bore Aether and Hemera.
summary_zh: 接下来，《神谱》说，黑夜和厄瑞玻斯相爱结合，黑夜怀孕，生下了埃忒耳和赫墨拉。

summary_en: Earth first bore starry Heaven, equal to herself, to cover her on every side and be an ever-sure abiding place for the blessed gods; she brought forth the long hills, graceful haunts of the nymphs who dwell in the glens; and she bore also the fruitless deep with its raging swell, Pontus, without sweet union of love.
summary_zh: 大地首先生下了和她一样大的繁星点点的天空乌拉诺斯，让他把自己完全覆盖，作为众神永远稳固的居所；她又生下了高高的群山，那是住在山谷里的仙女们喜爱的地方；她还不经过爱情，生下了波涛汹涌的荒凉大海蓬托斯。

summary_en: After telling how Cronos maimed Heaven and how Aphrodite was born of the sea-foam, the Theogony turns back to Night.
summary_zh: 在讲完克洛诺斯怎样阉割天空、阿佛洛狄忒怎样从海沫中诞生之后，《神谱》回到了黑夜身上。

summary_en: Next Hesiod tells of the family of Pontus, the Sea.
summary_zh: 接下来，赫西俄德讲大海蓬托斯的家族。

summary_en: After the daughters of Ocean and the rivers, the Theogony says: Theia, subject in love to Hyperion, bore great Helios and clear Selene and Eos, who shines upon all that are on earth and upon the deathless gods who live in wide heaven.
summary_zh: 在讲完大洋的女儿们和河流之后，《神谱》说：忒亚和许珀里翁相爱结合，生下了伟大的太阳赫利俄斯、明亮的月亮塞勒涅和黎明厄俄斯——厄俄斯为大地上的一切生灵、也为住在宽阔天空中的不死的神照亮道路。

summary_en: Next the Theogony says: Eurybia, bright among goddesses, was joined in love with Crius and bore great Astraeus, and Pallas, and Perses, who was eminent among all men in wisdom.
summary_zh: 紧接着，《神谱》说：欧律比亚，女神中光彩照人的一位，与克利俄斯相爱结合，生下了伟大的阿斯特赖俄斯、帕拉斯，还有在所有人中以智慧出众的珀耳塞斯。

summary_en: Then the poet says: Eos, a goddess, bore to Astraeus, a god, the strong-hearted winds — brightening Zephyrus, swift Boreas and Notus — in union of love.
summary_zh: 接着，诗人说：黎明女神厄俄斯和阿斯特赖俄斯——一位女神和一位神——在爱中结合，生下了心意强壮的风：吹得天空晴朗的西风仄费洛斯、迅猛的北风玻瑞阿斯和南风诺托斯。

summary_en: Styx, daughter of Ocean, was joined with Pallas and bore Zelos and trim-ankled Nike — Rivalry and Victory — in the house, and also Kratos and Bia — Strength and Force — wonderful children.
summary_zh: 大洋的女儿斯梯克斯与帕拉斯结合，在自己的宫殿里生下了泽洛斯和脚踝美丽的尼刻——竞争与胜利，又生下了克拉托斯和比亚——力量与暴力，这两个孩子都非常出色。

summary_en: King Gylfi of Sweden came to Ásgarðr and put his questions to the three seated on high thrones — High, Just-as-high and Third.
summary_zh: 瑞典国王古鲁菲来到阿斯加尔德，向坐在三个高座上的“至高者”“同样高者”和“第三者”提问。

summary_en: High said: the earth is circular, and around it lies the deep sea.
summary_zh: 至高者说：大地是圆的，四周环绕着深深的海洋。

summary_en: Just-as-high said: as the sons of Borr walked along the shore they found two logs and picked them up and made people of them.
summary_zh: 同样高者说：博尔的儿子们沿着海岸走，发现了两根树干，就拿起它们，用它们造出了人。
title_en: The first people and Odin's household

summary_en: Just-as-high went on: there was a giant living in Jötunheimr called Nörfi or Narfi.
summary_zh: 同样高者接着说：住在巨人国的一个巨人名叫纳尔菲，他有一个女儿叫夜，诺特。
uncertainty_note: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第9章称约尔德为奥丁之女，第10章称她为夜与安纳尔之女，两说并存。

summary_en: Gylfi asked how the sun and moon are steered.
summary_zh: 古鲁菲问：太阳和月亮是怎样运行的？

summary_en: Gylfi said: the sun moves fast, almost as if she were afraid; she could not go faster if she feared for her life.
summary_zh: 古鲁菲说：太阳跑得飞快，好像害怕什么，就算她怕死，也不会跑得更快了。
title_en: The wolves that chase sun and moon

summary_en: Third went on: first of all there was a world in the southern region called Muspell.
summary_zh: 第三者接着说：最先存在的，是南方的一个世界，叫做穆斯佩尔。

summary_en: Gylfi asked how things were before generations of men came to be.
summary_zh: 古鲁菲问：在人类出现以前，世界是什么样子？

summary_en: High went on: when the drops of melting rime were quickened by the power of the heat, they took the shape of a man, who is called Ymir; the frost-giants call him Aurgelmir, and from him are descended all the families of frost-giants.
summary_zh: 至高者接着说：融化的霜滴在热力的作用下有了生命，变成了一个人的形状，他名叫尤弥尔，霜巨人们叫他奥尔格尔米尔，所有的霜巨人都是他的后代。

summary_en: Gylfi asked where Ymir lived and what he lived on.
summary_zh: 古鲁菲问：尤弥尔住在哪里，靠什么活着？

summary_en: High went on: Búri begot a son called Borr.
summary_zh: 至高者接着说：布里有了一个儿子，名叫博尔。

summary_en: Gylfi asked whether there was peace between them or not.
summary_zh: 古鲁菲问：他们之间是和睦相处，还是互相敌对？

summary_en: Gylfi asked what the sons of Borr did then, if they are to be believed gods.
summary_zh: 古鲁菲问：如果你们认为博尔的儿子们是神，那他们后来做了什么？

summary_en: Third said: they also took his skull and made the sky from it, set it up over the earth with four points, and under each corner put a dwarf, named Austri, Vestri, Norðri and Suðri — East, West, North and South.
summary_zh: 第三者说：他们又拿起尤弥尔的头骨，用它造成天空，把它架在大地的上方，四个角各让一个矮人撑着，这四个矮人的名字是奥斯特里、韦斯特里、诺尔德里和苏德里——东、西、北、南。

summary_en: Skáldskaparmál 17 tells: Thor had gone east to fight trolls, and Óðinn rode Sleipnir into Jötunheimr and came to a giant called Hrungnir.
summary_zh: 《诗语法》第17章讲道：索尔到东方去打巨怪了，奥丁骑着他的八足马斯莱普尼尔来到巨人国，去拜访一个名叫赫朗格尼尔的巨人。

summary_en: Thjálfi went to Thor and tried to lift Hrungnir's leg off him, but could not.
summary_zh: 提亚尔菲走到索尔身边，想把赫朗格尼尔的腿从他身上搬开，可是怎么也搬不动。

summary_en: Thor went home to Þrúðvangar, and the whetstone remained stuck in his head.
summary_zh: 索尔回到了他的家斯鲁德万加尔，可是那块磨石还嵌在他的头里。

summary_en: Thor wanted to make Gróa glad, so he told her some news.
summary_zh: 索尔想让格罗亚高兴，就告诉她一个消息。

summary_en: Hrungnir rode in through the gods' gate, and when he came to the hall doors the Æsir invited him in to drink.
summary_zh: 赫朗格尼尔骑马冲进了众神的城门，他来到大殿门口时，阿萨神族的众神邀请他进去喝酒。

summary_en: Hrungnir got drunk and began to boast.
summary_zh: 赫朗格尼尔喝醉了，说起了大话。

summary_en: When the gods had had enough of his boasting they called on the name of Thor.
summary_zh: 众神听够了他的狂言，就喊出了索尔的名字。

summary_en: Hrungnir galloped back to Jötunheimr.
summary_zh: 赫朗格尼尔骑马飞奔回巨人国。

summary_en: Hrungnir himself had a famous heart: it was made of hard stone, spiky and three-cornered, like the carved symbol that has since been called Hrungnir's heart.
summary_zh: 赫朗格尼尔自己的心则是出了名的：它是用坚硬的石头做的，有棱有角，是三角形的，后来人们刻的一种叫做“赫朗格尼尔之心”的符号，就是照着它的样子画的。

summary_en: Thor went to the duel with his servant Thjálfi.
summary_zh: 索尔带着他的仆人提亚尔菲前去决斗。

summary_en: Then Hrungnir saw lightning and heard great thunderclaps, and he saw Thor in his godly wrath.
summary_zh: 接着，赫朗格尼尔看见了闪电，听见了巨大的雷声，然后他看见了索尔带着神的愤怒而来。

summary_en: While Thor fought Hrungnir, Thjálfi attacked the clay giant Mökkurkálfi.
summary_zh: 就在索尔和赫朗格尼尔交手的同时，提亚尔菲向泥巨人默库尔卡尔菲发起了攻击。

summary_en: In Snorri's Gylfaginning, High tells Gylfi about each of the Æsir.
summary_zh: 在斯诺里的《欺骗古鲁菲》里，至高者向古鲁菲一一介绍阿萨神族的众神。

summary_en: Loki presented his treasures first.
summary_zh: 洛基先献上他的宝物。

summary_en: Then Brokkr presented his treasures.
summary_zh: 接着，勃洛克献上他的宝物。

summary_en: Loki offered to redeem his head, but the dwarf said there was no hope of that.
summary_zh: 洛基提出要用钱赎回自己的头，可矮人说没有这回事。

summary_en: Skáldskaparmál 35 begins with a question: why is gold called Sif's hair?
summary_zh: 《诗语法》第35章从一个问题开始：为什么金子被称为“希芙的头发”？

summary_en: When Thor found his wife's hair shorn, he seized Loki and would have broken every bone in his body.
summary_zh: 索尔发现妻子的头发被剪光后，立刻抓住了洛基。

summary_en: So Loki went to the dwarves called the sons of Ívaldi.
summary_zh: 洛基于是去找那些被称为伊瓦尔迪之子的矮人。

summary_en: Loki took the treasures and wagered his head with a dwarf called Brokkr that his brother Eitri — called Sindri in some manuscripts and later writers — could not make three treasures as good as these.
summary_zh: 洛基拿着宝物，找到一个名叫勃洛克的矮人，跟他打赌，把自己的头押上：他说勃洛克的兄弟埃特里——有些抄本和后人叫他辛德里——不可能打造出三件和这三件一样好的宝物。

summary_en: Eitri laid a pigskin in the forge and told Brokkr to blow the bellows and not stop until he took out what he had put in.
summary_zh: 埃特里把一张猪皮放进炉子里，吩咐勃洛克拉风箱，在他把东西从炉子里取出来以前，一刻也不许停下。

summary_en: Next Eitri laid gold in the forge and bade Brokkr blow and not stop until he came back.
summary_zh: 接着，埃特里把金子放进炉子里，又吩咐勃洛克拉风箱，在他回来以前不许停下。

summary_en: Last, Eitri laid iron in the forge and told Brokkr he must keep blowing or everything would be spoiled.
summary_zh: 最后，埃特里把铁放进炉子里，对勃洛克说，必须一直拉风箱，否则一切都会毁掉。

summary_en: Brokkr came to Ásgarðr with his treasures, and Loki brought the treasures of the sons of Ívaldi.
